We visited Austin for the weekend and decided to try this place for the first time. Everything lived up to the hype! The meat was fresh, high quality, and perfectly seasoned, and the homemade tortillas made the tacos even better.
Be prepared to wait in line because this place is always busy, but it's absolutely worth it. The carne Asada taco was delicious and definitely worth the wait. The service was excellent as well. After ordering at the cashier, our food came out quickly.
If you're visiting Austin, this spot is a must-try. We can't wait to come back the next time we're in town!

This is definitely a spot to grab food, it was delicious. They open at 11:30 and I arrived near that time and it was already getting busy. There wasn’t a wait to order when I went, I didn’t wait much to get the food either the cooks were very fast. The entire staff was very welcoming and friendly super nice people! I order tacos campechanos (they are not stingy with the meat they were pretty stuffed). The tacos were delicious I added more red salsa and it was good the spice wasn’t extreme but every salsa I tried was good each had plenty of flavor that just added to the tacos. My fiancé ordered a campechano burrito and it was delicious his feedback was that it is one of the best burritos he’s had in a while, I agree. Though I didn’t get a picture of the burrito it was a pretty big size it was definitely stuffed. They have options on drinks I ordered agua de horchata but they also have agua de Jamaica, and options on sodas and bottled water. The horchata was so good it was very smooth and sweet but not overly sweet where it just taste like sugar.
Everything is definitely 10/10!

text.text:
Upon entering, patrons are immediately transported to the vibrant culinary scene of Mexico. This establishment serves authentic Mexican cuisine, devoid of any Tex-Mex influences.
Despite the presence of a lengthy queue, patrons should not be discouraged, as the service is remarkably swift and efficient.
It is important to note that the tortillas served are exceptionally large. Corn tortillas are approximately three times the size of standard street tacos, while flour tortillas are also significantly larger than the average.
Even on a Thursday evening, the establishment maintains a lively atmosphere with two Al Pastor trompas spinning.
Seating arrangements can be somewhat challenging, but patrons typically do not linger for extended periods.
Ultimately, the tacos offered are remarkably flavorful. Additionally, the establishment provides bottle Coke. While the tacos may be on the pricier side, their substantial size justifies the cost.

text.text:
One of the best bites of food I’ve ever had.

My wife found this place after we walked nearly 20K steps by noon in Austin. Upon arrival, this is definitely almost a “taco speakeasy” trying to find it! It’s in an alley that you then walk into from the back and walk behind the kitchen to get in line. Such an interesting setup!

You’re on top of everyone there, but the music loudly playing, the good smells, smiling faces, the decorative vent hood…you know you’re in for a good time!

We ordered two carne asada burritos with cheese (one without beans and one with beans). We also ordered chips and salsa and a side of cactus (nopales).

Every single bite was incredibly delicious. The salsa packed tons of flavor that left elements of spice in every bite. Not too heavy on spice or one flavor more specifically. Tons of depth and every bite tasted like the first. The chips were not overly oily like some other places. Very fresh and warm!

The burrito though was on another level. That homemade tortilla they wrap the burrito in delectable. Buttery, soft and melts in you mouth while still substantially holding all of the ingredients just showcases they have a substantially quality product.

They loaded this burrito with carne asada. Great amount of filling and the carne asada has a great flavor profile.

Overall, this place is actually named. One of the best bites of food I’ve ever had. Cannot recommend this place enough. If I’m in Austin, I’ll find myself a way to come back here!

text.text:
We had a spontaneous date night on a Thursday and hit up Vespaio after our favorite mezcal bar “El Chapulin” next door recommended it. We didn’t have a reservation and were initially told we could snatch a seat at the bar as it is first come first serve. We waited about 5 minutes before realizing it wasn’t going to be available anytime soon. We went back to the host and asked if we could be put down on the list for the next available table. It was going to be a 2 hour wait but we were going to hit up some stores to kill some time. Just as we were walking out the door, the host called us back to let us know that a cocktail table next to the bar was just now available and that it was open seating and we would have a server. Of course we took it!

As soon as sat down, they brought us some water and two menus. It was a bit loud but we could still make conversation without feeling like we were yelling. We were just overhearing everyone else’s conversations. Our server checked in and made some suggestions.

We ordered a Caesar salad and calamari to start which came out quickly. They split the Caesar salad into two plates which was a nice touch. The calamari was delicious, although I wish it was a little more crispy as it would fall apart as you grabbed it. The Caesar salad was okay, not anything special as I’ve had better.

We shared a pizza for our first plate and the server had recommended the hot honey pizza which was so good! It is brick oven baked and full of flavor and perfectly crispy. We ended up splitting the lasagna and it is massive! It was deliciously cheesy and the marinara was so flavorful! We both almost finished it and that is how good it is!

I definitely recommend making a reservation to avoid the wait and the noisey bar area with very tight walking space. I felt like people would walk by about 2 inches away from us and that’s how tight it is but for the convenience of not waiting it was worth it. Parking is street parking on south Congress but we were lucky to have found one about 2 blocks away. We enjoyed the walk to and from the restaurant so it wasn’t a problem.

Overall we enjoyed our dinner date and were fulfilled, literally and figuratively! We highly recommend this spot!

We bid farewell to Vespaio last night. Our server Daniel was the highlight of the meal. Witty, welcoming, kind and funny. He started there a year ago this month. I hope he lands at another wonderful restaurant where he can shine.

Food was beyond delicious and the company even better. A couple of footnotes from us being we've been here many times over the years - no white table clothes (which gives a soft touch) and it was exceptionally loud which we just don't recall that ever being. It was packed to the rim. But we had our little corner in paradise. And Daniel was super attentive and knew his stuff. Ask for him if you can!

We started with split a Caesar salad - and those homemade croutons! Do NOT leave one behind whatever you do!

We also split a delicious bottle of 2019 Bourdeaux.

Shared grilled broccoli, pecorino with our primi of:

TAGLIATELLE CON FUNGHI & 1/2 order of BUTTERNUT SQUASH PANSOTTI

I may try to slip in to the bar side for a final happy hour before officially saying arrivederci.

We went to Two Hands for brunch on a Sunday.  It was busy, but not overcrowded, and we had a reservation!

We started with Crispy Brussels Spouts and they were defininitely a favorite and so delicious!  The tables on either side of us ordered the Brussels as well!

I had the Two Hander Burger and it was great.  Very good Montana Waygu beef!  It comes with shoestring style french fries that reminded me of my childhood and were so crisp and tasty (see picture!). We also had the Salmon Quinoa Bowl which is a tasty, healthy choice, salmon was terrific.
The Steak and Egg was quality.  The steak was slightly underseasoned but the French anchovy dressing more than made up for it!  The hashbrowns and egg were both great with it!  Lastly, we had the Smashed Avo Toast with smoked Salmon and it was wonderful.
Also recommend the Hot Vanilla Orange Blossom Latte and for dessert, the Banana Walnut Bread topped with Espresso Mascarpone, so decadent!

Add-on for my meal was forgotten.  I had to request it be taken off the tab. The food was good, no complaints on that.  I just don't think it was worth the price.  It is in a trendy spot right on touristy South Congress, so I guess that can be justification for mark ups.

I live locally and have had much better service here before but this negative experience makes me feel uncomfortable returning or recommending to others.

text.text:
My Absolute Favorite Spot in Austin – Beer, Kolaches, and Community!

Batch Craft Beer & Kolaches is hands down my favorite place in the city; I find myself coming here several times a week! It is incredibly family-friendly—you’ll always see parents relaxing with their kids or babies in the massive backyard. It’s the perfect spot to soak in the Austin weather and that uniquely chill "Austin vibe."

What sets Batch apart is their commitment to live music. With both indoor and outdoor stages, there is almost always something amazing happening. I recently caught a Tango performance there that was so authentic, I felt like I had been transported straight to Argentina! I also love that they support Anthropos Arts, a local nonprofit for music education, by hosting student performances once a month.

Beyond the atmosphere, the quality of their craft beer, coffee, and kolaches is consistently top-tier. It is rare to find a place that excels at all three while remaining so community-focused. Whether you’re a local or just visiting, this multifaceted gem is something you simply cannot miss. 10/10 for the food, the music, and the heart!

text.text:
Jeffrey’s has been a regular stop for us, and Easter brunch added a new dimension to an already well-established favorite.

Everything about the experience felt intentional. The brunch menu struck exactly the right balance, familiar enough to feel like a proper Sunday meal, but with enough creativity to keep every course interesting. Nothing felt forced or overwrought. Just confident, well-executed food.

The drinks program is equally impressive. Whether you’re going mimosas or something more creative, the bar delivers. And the desserts, genuinely divine. The kind that make you reconsider whether you actually needed to save room.

What elevates Jeffrey’s above the crowd, though, is the service. Impeccable is the right word. Attentive without hovering, knowledgeable without being precious. You feel like a guest, not a table to turn.
Austin has no shortage of places competing for “best in the city,” but Jeffrey’s has earned that conversation. We keep coming back for a reason, and Easter brunch only confirmed it.

text.text:
Loro has quickly become one of my favorite places to eat. The first time I went was with a group of friends, and everything we ordered was incredible. There was even a wedding dinner of some sort and they surprised us with some complimentary appetizers, not sure if it was related, but it was definitely a nice touch and honestly made the experience even better.

The setup is a little different than a typical restaurant you order at the bar instead of with a waiter, and then they bring the food out to your table. They have both bar seating and regular dining tables, and there's plenty of indoor and outdoor seating depending on the weather and time of the day.

I've been back a second time by myself, and to no surprised the food was just as good. I also love that they switch things up with new menu items and different drinks every so often, so there's always something new to try. The staff has been super friendly every visit too.

The only real "challenge" is parking since it's usually pretty packed, but I've always been able to find a spot in the back after a short walk. Definitely worth it, I will definitely be coming back. If you're thinking about trying Loro, DO it you won't regret it.

text.text:
Pros: plenty of seating, outdoor seating, amazing meats, fantastic brussels sprouts, great yuzu soda
Cons: essentially no parking, very loud

Their turkey breast was some of the best turkey I've ever had in my life. Tender, moist, flavorful, smokey, savory. The Brussels sprouts were also really good—perfectly charred on the outside, great sauteed flavor. The Bangkok Spicy Chicken bowl was less impressive, but still good; it wasn't spicy at all, but I did like the kaarage chicken, the coconut lime rice, and the dry, crunchy “slaw” (more like plain julienned raw papaya) was ok. Their yuzu soda is outstanding. Inside it was so loud I had trouble hearing anyone, outside was more manageable, particularly in the back where the parking is.

Really cool restaurant concept. Food is great. Fighting for parking is just not worth it though.

text.text:
Paperboy is a fantastic brunch spot in Austin! From the moment we arrived, the atmosphere was welcoming and inviting, and the staff was incredibly friendly and attentive.

We tried several dishes, and everything was delicious. The migas with eggs were flavorful and perfectly cooked. The fried chicken biscuit was outstanding, crispy, juicy, and packed with flavor. We also ordered the red salsa chilaquiles with carnitas, and they were absolutely amazing.

For something sweet, we shared a plain pancake and a blueberry pancake. Both were light, fluffy, and delicious.

They also offer a great selection of coffee drinks and cocktails. I had a cappuccino, which was good, but the food was definitely the highlight of our visit.

Overall, Paperboy delivers great food, a lovely atmosphere, and excellent service. I highly recommend it, and I will definitely be coming back. If you’re looking for a great brunch spot in Austin, this place is a must-visit!.

My wife and I had breakfast at Paperboy South. Though in a busy area, the outside patio (where we sat) was stylishly well-bordered and quiet enough to easily hear table talk.

My wife ordered a Kale Salad and I had a Classic Breakfast.  Inside Tip - the $3 upcharge to replace the potato wedges with the Cheddar Hashbrown is well worth it!

My wife loved the Kale Salad - the poached egg and the salad were great. The Classic Breakfast was so tasty. The maple sausage patty was delicious and the toast was thick enough to sop up egg yolks.

Our Server Daniel was excellent. Quick, friendly and informative.

I recommend Paperboy South for anyone's breakfast needs. You won't be disappointed.

The lox is large and moist and goes well with the salt of the bagel and the light seasoning on the onion. The salad is the same gem lettuce salad in the restaurant that I love.

So this is yes a review of the coffee and of the vibe but really of that lox-and-bagel.

If you’re vegetarian or vegan, be careful with this place. I found a piece of meat in my bagel. This is the first time I’ve experienced such negligence, and it’s honestly disgusting.

It seems like they may have started preparing a meat bagel, then realized I ordered a classic egg and cheese without any meat. Instead of using a new bagel, they probably thought it wouldn’t matter, the customer don't get it and just used the same one anyway.

I will never eat here again. It’s not hard to respect people’s dietary choices. I’m really disappointed.

Check the other comments, they've done this before. People have reported issues with cross-contamination, and even the manager said, “there’s bacon flying everywhere.” If you’re careful about your dietary restrictions for ethical or personal reasons, you should definitely avoid this place.

Had heard rave reviews from my daughter and her friends who frequent regularly and was excited to try. Was sadly very underwhelmed. Took a bite of her Longhorn on an Everything bagel with bacon and the seeds on the bagel were burnt and honestly the sandwich was nothing special. I got the pastrami hash on sesame and did not care much for it either - the hash was under-seasoned which may be bec pastrami is salty but there was too little pastrami and too much pickled jalapeno which just overpowered the whole sandwich. I honestly didn’t even check if there was cheese bec I didn’t taste it. Servers were extremely nice though, and efficiently worked through the wall-to-wall Saturday morning crowd. And it sure was packed (we probably waited 20+ mins) which also made for a loud and claustrophobic meal, so we took it to go instead.

If I ever return, I think I’ll just get a bagel and cream cheese bec the sandwiches were just sadly, a let down, especially for the $12/sandwich price tag. Lots of other breakfast and brunch places in town with far better food and value.

We also went a little crazy and ordered the Longhorn (2 fried eggs, cheddar cheese, breakfast potatoes, Charlie's hot sauce, and we chose the vegan sausage) which was heavy and decadent and wonderful. They were both really really good. An excellent bagel place, indeed.

This was my first time visiting this establishment. I initially expected it to be more of a traditional sit-down restaurant, but upon entering I realized it’s actually a self-ordering setup. Customers place their orders at one of the two kiosks on the side, and then receive a text message when their food is ready for pickup at the window.

I do wish it had more of a sit-down dining experience rather than the ordering system they use. However, the food itself was very good. The biscuit was moist and flavorful, and I especially enjoyed the bacon. I also had orange juice, which paired well with the meal.

Overall, I would recommend this place because the food is great, but the ordering setup isn’t my personal preference.

text.text: I’d heard about this place for quite a while before coming here and it was very different than what I was expecting. This is essentially a food truck in a really large seating area next to a bar and the outdoor theater. I imagine in the middle of summer, it would be uncomfortably hot, as there is no indoor seating, but the weather was perfect when we were there. It’s an interesting place where you can bring your dogs and the line is a bit long but people here come out and answer questions about what’s on the menu so it doesn’t take too long. You get in line immediately when you get into the area and then you order and they give you a number and will bring the food to you. If you want drinks, you walk to the bar about 10 m away, which fortunately had no line at all. This is a fun location and very Austin. The menu is relatively small. Basically you order the sauce that you want on their handmade pasta, and then you add whatever else you want to add in, like meatballs. There are a few side dishes, like garlic, bread, and salads, and the food was great. If you were coming here expecting this to be like Mandola‘s or the Olive Garden, it is very different. If you want to go to a quirky Austin place, this is it.

4.2 stars
First of all, be prepared to have patience as this place had a huge line on a Sunday night. The guy that was running the orders was super nice. He gave good recs and even gave us free beets (bc we are indecisive and were between tomatoes and beets for the $55 abbi dish). The food took around 9 minutes to come out for the salads, tomatoes, beets, and garlic bread. The salad was pretty good (italian salad) but was quite strange how there were just chunks of garlic tossed in there (like whole cloves). The beets were decent, but the tomatoes are much much better tbh. The garlic bread honestly needed a bit more love; it is quite overhyped. If only it were hotter when it came out, had butter, and  cheese (then it would be perfect!). The stars of the show came out after: pomodoro pasta (very good!), cacio e pepe (mid!), and the pesto pasta (so so fire!). The chicken in tomato sauce was actually insane (get it!!). It comes with two pieces for the duo plate thing. My friend ordered a carbonara and hated it. It was not good tbh; it had a weird cheese mixed in with it. Otherwise, my final plea to the creative staff: bring fettuccine alfredo in place of the cacio e pepe PLEASE! Also a bolognese pasta!! Love the people that work here and the ambience! Will come back.

text.text:
Emmer & Rye absolutely delivered. We had dinner there on July 3rd while in Austin, and it was one of those meals where every course felt thoughtful, creative, and completely dialed in.

We started with the smoked Gulf oyster, which had this awesome balance of smoke, brightness, and heat. It was bold without being heavy, and a perfect way to kick things off. The sourdough bread was ridiculous in the best way — great texture, deeply flavorful, and that cultured butter with smoked blackberry honey took it over the top.

The tortelloni was probably one of my favorite bites of the night. Rich, savory, and beautifully balanced, with just enough uniqueness to make it memorable without feeling like it was trying too hard. The arepa was another standout — comforting, buttery, and full of flavor. Simple idea, executed at a very high level.

Then came the Texas Akaushi wagyu, and it was exactly what you hope for when you order wagyu in Texas: perfectly cooked, deeply beefy, tender, and paired with flavors that complemented the meat instead of covering it up.

Dessert was a fig pudding-style dish, and I wish I remembered the exact name because it was fantastic. Fresh figs, glossy syrupy sweetness, beautiful texture, and just enough richness to finish the meal on a high note without feeling overdone.

Service was excellent, the pacing was smooth, and the whole experience had that rare mix of creativity, hospitality, and serious culinary skill. Emmer & Rye is easily one of the best meals we’ve had in Austin, and I’d go back in a heartbeat.

Finally able to try Emmer & Rye. Customer service was superb.  They even changed my plate after the appetizers without me having to ask. :) The place itself was nice too, and since the weather was great, we sat out on the patio.

For appetizers, we got the empanada, which was okay, the flavor leaned more Mexican than Peruvian. Our server suggested pairing it with the tomato and honeydew dish, and that turned out to be a great recommendation. Everything sat on top of a curry sauce that surprisingly worked really well together.

For mains, we had the gulf fish and the pork loin with black chow chow, which I really liked. The pork was moist with a crust.  Overall, it was a great experience. They rotate the menu often, so we may come back to try again.

Unfortunately, they didn’t have a chocolate dessert that appealed to me, so I skipped dessert. One thing to note: the portions are on the smaller side, so you may want to order more dishes than you normally would.

Staff was welcoming, friendly and helpful as a 1st timer.

Can’t wait to come back soon!

If you’re anywhere near Austin, do yourself a favor and stop by NADC Burger.

I’ll be honest—I was skeptical at first. Dropping nearly $19 on a burger had me questioning the decision. But the second I took that first bite, it all made sense. This isn’t just a burger—it’s a proper burger. The flavor, the quality, the way everything comes together… it hits on every level.

The patty was cooked perfectly, the balance of toppings was dialed in, and you can tell they don’t cut corners. It’s one of those meals where halfway through you’re already thinking about when you’re coming back.

Even though I don’t live in Austin, this is absolutely a spot I’ll recommend to anyone heading there. It exceeded expectations in every way.

Bottom line: yeah, it’s pricey—but it’s worth every dollar.

My only critique involves the sports-viewing experience. We specifically came to watch the Spurs game and mentioned that to the hostess when we arrived. While I understand Uptown Sports Club isn’t a traditional sports bar, we weren’t seated in an area where we could comfortably watch the game and ultimately ended up leaving to find another venue.

What made this especially puzzling was the large screen on the back patio. It wasn’t being used, and that space was never offered as an option despite our stated reason for visiting. Given the venue’s name and the obvious potential of that setup, it felt like a missed opportunity and, frankly, a bit shortsighted.

That said, the food, drinks, atmosphere, and service were all outstanding. I’d happily return for those reasons alone and hope the management leans a little more into the “sports” part of Uptown Sports Club in the future.

text.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

If you’re planning to visit Toasty Badger, just know that even if you make an online reservation, seating is still first come, first served when you arrive. There also isn’t really a place to wait inside, so be prepared if you’re visiting on a hot Texas day.

Once we got inside, though, everything changed for the better! We ended up with the perfect seats at the bar, which gave us a fun, old-school diner experience.

The food was absolutely amazing. One tip: order just one pancake to share! They’re gigantic and literally take up an entire plate. We also loved the mimosa flight—it was exactly what we needed and a fun way to try different flavors.

The staff was top-notch. From the moment we were seated, everyone was friendly, attentive, and genuinely wanted to make sure we had a great first experience. They checked on us throughout our meal and made us feel very welcome.

The wait outside in the heat wasn’t ideal, but the food, drinks, and outstanding service made it completely worth it. We’ll definitely be back!

text.text:
Had brunch here with a friend of mine who was in town from San Antonio. I’ve always passed by this place and have seen a line out the door so thought we would try it since it seemed “slow” on a Tuesday. The seats inside are quite tight and so you can hear other conversations right next to you. It also seems like others are listening in on your convos so if that is an issue I would suggest sitting outside. The inside is decorated really cute but it’s cozy with limited amount of tables.

When I looked at the Google reviews, I craved the pancakes so that’s what I ended up ordering. I didn’t realize the pancakes only come alone so you have to order any sides à la carte. My friend ordered the turkey sandwich which she describes as “sweet and salty” and it comes with fries and a chocolate dip. My pancakes came out looking super light and I was concerned they weren’t fully cooked thoroughly but they actually were. I would rate the pancakes a 7/10. They have a nice texture but they are more on the salty side. Not my style for pancakes but to each their own. The bacon was nice and crispy.

Our server quickly attended us but also seemed to forget about us after we ordered. I had to ask another server for a coffee refill. The table next to us also had to take their cups by the bar to get our servers attention for refills. She did come out with their refills and was apologetic. It might’ve been a shift change and she was probably stuck doing side work.

I would say it does seem overpriced for the value and quantity you get. Parking is tough and my friend had to park down the street by Wells Fargo. I might bring my husband here to try it out but probably won’t be our go-to spot. Especially if they have a long wait.

text.text:
Overall: 4.1/5

Came on a Wednesday morning and there was no line so I got my order right away. None of the pastries had any strong or overwhelming flavors which I appreciated.

BBQ Pork Rib Kolache ($5.75): Delicious and probably my favorite of the three.

Churro and Dulce De Leche Star ($4.50): This was my least favorite. It tasted like a regular sugar donut with just a hint of churro flavor.

Horchata Donut ($4.85): Yum. It wasn't sweet and had a beautiful meringue on top. Just know the meringue will melt in the heat. The texture was softer than the churro and dulce de leche star which I preferred.

Pistachio Butter Latte ($8.75) + Oat Milk ($1.25): The cashier recommended this one and it was really unique. You need to stir it for a while since the butter on top is pretty thick. It wasn't sweet at first but as you keep sipping and stirring the sweetness from the pistachio starts coming through. I enjoyed it but it is heavier than your usual latte and I couldn't finish it all in one sitting.

text.text: This is my new favorite brunch spot in Austin hands down! It was so good we went back 2 times in a week. The scrambled egg with roti, potato hash, and the breakfast burger were all 10/10. Also, you HAVE to ask for the house-made ketchup!!!! It took me by surprise because i wasn’t expecting much, but i was so close to asking if they sell it! A must if you like ketchup with your brunch. The flavors are unique and creative while still being absolutely delicious. The coffee is amazing too. The aussie iced coffee comes with ice cream and once you mix it in it’s the perfect amount of sweetness. Cappuccino is also a 10/10. They usually sell out of their baked goods by the late afternoon, but we got the carrot cake with this amazing cream cheese icing and it was not too sweet and hit the spot after having all the savory food. Parking is very easy, they have a parking lot right outside or you can get your parking validated for the parking garage right next to it, which is always pretty empty. I’m recommending Proud Mary’s to everyone i know, it’s that good! Highly recommend!

text.text: One of our favorite places. We’ve dined here several times throughout the years and have enjoyed it very much. To celebrate life and also just because. The atmosphere is warm and cozy inside and the wine garden is nicely lit up. While I would say I am not typically a fan of a rotating menu, I thoroughly enjoy the change up here. (Although if I say so myself the squash, crawfish pasta, beef cheek with mushrooms, and honey pie are very missed!!! Bring back anytime! 😆) We did the tasting menu our very first time, but it works best for us to just order 4-5 things off the menu that we find interesting and unique. We always ask our server as well and we’ve never been misguided. The pullman bread is a classic that is always enjoyed every time. Crab fingers and hushpuppies are also menu staples that are good and seem to be available year round. We also enjoy the red wine selection they have. Most recently we had the roasted chili lime chicken and the sweet potato gnocchi which was great! We would 100% recommend and will be back.

No wonder this place is hard to get into! We snagged a last minute reservation on a day where temps were dropping in the evening, but were still able to enjoy their lovely patio with all the heat lamps.
Great wine based cocktails and a fun wine list. Loved the smoky drink especially and the orange wine from Chile 🧡🔥
We were recommended 3-5 dishes for 2 people and ended up ordering 5 because we couldn’t decide. At least something on the menu changes every 3 weeks, so won’t describe every dish. BUT, EVERYTHING that we ordered we would get again! It’s been a while since that has happened, especially in Austin. Just wow on all the flavors, textures and acidity balance.
Cannot wait to return and maybe get to the desert the time…the basque cheesecake has our name on it, but we were too full! Will just have to come back within 3 weeks!

text.text:
Golden Hour Café  & Wine Bar is an absolute gem! From the moment you walk in, you're welcomed by a cozy, quiet, and modern atmosphere that's perfect for relaxing with friends or enjoying a date night. I brought my cousin here when she was in town and she can't wait to visit it again the next time she's here!

One of our favorite things is their rotating menu.... there's always something new and delicious to try. Their weekly wine flights are such a fun experience, giving you the chance to sample 4–5 different wines from their impressive wine list. It's the perfect way to discover new favorites!

If you're looking for a warm, inviting spot with great food, exceptional wine, and a wonderful atmosphere, Golden Hour is a must-visit.

text.text: Hillside Farmacy has been on my list for quite some time and was finally able to visit…twice in 2 weeks because the food is that good! The owners Jade and Greg have done an excellent job of curating a delicious menu and transformed this old pharmacy into a cool atmosphere with the history of building still present. From the Farmacy Plate (meat and cheese board) and Arancini Balls as apps, I knew we were off to a great start!! For main courses, we ordered the Texas Wagyu Cheeseburger, Mushroom Pasta, and Steak Frites. My favorite of these was the mushroom pasta. I’m drooling again as I write this! Shoutout to Bird who is a fantastic server. She gave us great recommendations! Oh and I can’t forget the drinks! We ordered old fashioned drinks from the soda fountain, Hibiscus Lemonade and Turmeric Black Pepper on one trip and the Frozen Painkiller and Sandoval Daiquiri on the other. My words don’t do justice. You’ll just have to go and try it yourself. I have heard great things about their brunch too. I’d recommended getting reservations in advance because they fill up especially the patio on a nice day. Thanks Hillside Farmacy!!

text.text:
Food I had:

Swedish iced coffee & Smoked turkey Sandwich (no onion)

No hyperbole was used in writing this review.

When I took the first bite out of my smoked turkey sandwich, I thanked every god, of every religion, for allowing me to consume such a gift.

I’m not a big tomato guy. I’m not a big sandwich guy. This is no longer the case.

The Swedish hill smoked turkey sandwich has completely changed my view on what is possible regarding sandwiches.

The Swedish hill smoked turkey sandwich is a beautiful harmony of ingredients that does not care about you and your past. It will be the best sandwich you have ever had. It is the best sandwich. Period.

As far as the Swedish iced coffee goes.. this was an experience in it self. I am reviewing it apart from the sandwich.

This is peak iced coffee. I’ve only been on this planet for 23 years so maybe I’m not experienced to say this. But I believe this to be the pinnacle of coffee period. It actually tastes enough like coffee (somewhat bitter in the best way possible) but sweet (thanks to the oat milk and coconut cream). These two elements are combined in a way that allows the enjoyer the savor both sides, instead of simply having each part of the coffee combine and become one.

All of this to say, I had a great time. Please, if there is anything you do on your time on earth, try the Swedish hill smoked turkey sandwich and Swedish iced coffee. One have not fully lived until trying both.

JN

Ps I would’ve loved to wait a shorter amount of time for my order but I did go during peak times on a Saturday so I can’t complain.

text.text:
We came Here on a Thursday night around 8:30 PM. We wanted to sit on the patio, but for whatever reason it was closed

First off and most importantly, on our way out, we saw a roach on the floor near the host stand. I also saw another review that mentioned roaches. 🤢

We never received any chips and salsa when everybody else around us did. The crab queso was really good though that was the only thing we liked.

I ordered the la Diabla Margarita it tasted watered down, it was disappointing. My girlfriend ordered the watermelon frozen margarita she said it was just OK.

I ordered the ARRACHERA Which was lacking seasoning it wasn’t very flavorful and I make better steaks at home. My girlfriend ordered the tacos- the Pollo Asado, carne asada, and the fish. When they came out, they were pretty cold and dry. We asked for salsa, which made it a little better.

Overall, it was pretty disappointing and we will not come back. The location is nice and I’m sure that the rooftop Patio has great vibes, but that’s about it.

text.text:
I had a work lunch meeting here for my first visit! They have both indoor and outdoor seating but we chose to sit inside. You walk up to the counter to order and there are menus as you walk in.

You will also want to go to the iPads/kiosks to input your license plate to validate parking. They offer 3 free hours of parking!

I ordered a vanilla latte and my colleague ordered a dirty chai. Both were brought to our table and they were freshly made! I really liked the vanilla latte and it was the perfect temperature!

For lunch, it was cold outside so I went with their green pozole. Being Mexican, I was a bit nervous but wanted to give it a try. When it was brought out, I was pleasantly surprised. It looked interesting! I dove in and let me tell you… it was delicious!! All of the toppings come together for the perfect bite every time! There is plenty of shredded chicken which made it very fulfilling. I do wish there was more broth but it was still worth it!

My colleague finished her chicken biscuit and said it was yummy! She liked the spicy jalapeño sauce it comes with!

We were both fulfilled at the end of our meeting! I will definitely be back!! Highly recommend this spot!

This Uchi location for Austin was a fun dinner with friends that, while for sure was tasty and the aesthetic was on point, I just wasn't impressed enough to warrant the price tag.

I've been to plenty of other higher end sushi-styled restaurants and Uchiba is a solid addition to that established restaurant type, but nothing we received really wowed me.

The skewers were nice, but overly sticky. The sushi fresh, but that's the requirement. The dumplings solid, but oddly sweet when not desired.

Maybe we needed to try more options/we ordered the wrong mix, but I came away unimpressed food-wise. The service and vibes were awesome however.

text.text:
Cuantos Tacos is the kind of place that reminds you why Austin’s taco scene is so good. The bright yellow trailer, the simple setup, and the Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition all fit together: this is a place that feels casual and approachable, but the food clearly rises to a very high standard.
The tacos are the real reason to come. Cuantos Tacos focuses on Mexico City-style street tacos and is known for quality, value, and a tight menu that stays true to what it does best. The menu includes favorites like suadero, cachete, buche, carnitas, longaniza, costras, and quesadillas, with classic drinks like Jarritos and Coca-Cola Mexicana to round it out.
What stands out most is how unpretentious the whole experience feels. It’s a no-frills taco trailer, but the food and reputation make it feel like a genuine hidden gem rather than just another food stop. The prices are reasonable, the value is strong, and the experience feels memorable without trying too hard.
If you want excellent tacos in Austin and appreciate a place that earns its praise with quality instead of hype, Cuantos Tacos is absolutely worth a visit.

text.text:
Sigh - I wanted this place to be 5 stars. Here are the reasons why:
1. Celebration of Mexican cuisine and culture, but with a bit of flare. Perfect for 2026.
2. Stand out menu items. Classics not overly complicated sans the concha.
3. Customer service is warm and welcoming, they call you by your name as though they’ve known you for a while.
4. Parking - having parking is a big plus for restaurants and bakeries here in Austin, that automatically raises the score for me.
5. Love at first bite - again that Vanailla Concha is fantastic as well as the Polvorones. Not to mention the stand out flavor on a bean, egg, and cheese taco. Delicious first bites. The Masa Sugar Cookie is a star, not too sweet and that lovely corn flavor comes through nicely - this is from an anti-sugar cookie pov.

Here is why it’s a 3 star rating:
1. The Polvorones: while absolutely delicious, pecan shells ruined the experience. I’m not a fan of risking the integrity of my teeth and I’d be wary to order more again.
2. The Pink Cake: where’s the flavor? I assumed a corn-like base with a flavorful pink frosting would blow me away. Instead it was lard/butter like flavors. An absolute miss.
3. For the price, perfection is expected. This Panaderia seems like it prides itself on its quality and the accolades of the chef…yet there are notable disappointments in items that could be a knockout. The Polvoron was literally the best I’ve had in a LONG time and the pecan shells ruined it - Sigh

text.text:
This place has been on my list for over a year and last year I wasn’t able to stop by while visiting. About a week ago I listen to the chef/owner on the “she’s my cherry pie “ podcast and her passion and dedication to honoring her heritage and paying an affordable wage while being passionate about quality is impressive. $7.50 may be steep for a pastry but knowing the quality and effort that she puts into every item while paying affordable wages makes it understandable.

Anyway, This time it was a must visit on a quick over night trip.  I ended up not making it in till around 1230-1 so most stuff was gone but they had the seasonal strawberry sunflower seed concha which was what I wanted anyway.

The Concha had a nice crispy outside with a soft airy inside, the jam wasn’t too sweet and there was just enough sunflower to kiss your palate to let you know it was there.

I would have loved to try other items but what I did try was top notch. Hope to make it by again for more tasty treats soon.

text.text: We had a great experience here! My 3 & 6 yo daughters (and 3 mo son) and I went on a Friday night close to 5pm and the place was pretty empty (until about 20 minutes later). The atmosphere is so quaint and beautiful, the turfed field with a little tunnel, chalkboard, and sports balls was great for the littles, the snow cone place wasn't open but Besame and Veracruz were open til 8. From Veracruz we ordered the Al Pastor Taco, Grilled Fish Taco, and breakfast tacos (requested just bacon, egg & cheese) and they came out in a timely manner and were very tasty - the side sauces are a bit spicy but yum! From Besame we ordered the Mint Cookie Monster and some coffee flavored one I can't remember the name of and they were both delicious! Kind of pricey though, the kid size is $5.75 for like one scoop. The staff at both places were friendly and answered any questions. There is a bathroom located outside of the fenced area in the apartment complex, and parking is not great, although when we went we didn't have any issues. If we lived closer, we would definitely frequent this place more often!

text.text:
This place is unbelievably good, the only people I wouldn’t recommend this place to would be those with little self restraint. As I’ve definitely had to pry myself away a few times. I’ve had a majority of the menu (the pastry/sweet side) and every single one is SO flaky, and decadent. The visible layers of pastry, the gorgeous coating and color. I myself would recommend the Kouign-amann and literally any of their croissants specifically. Before coming in, I’d never heard of a Kouign-amann, and let me say they’ve set the bar very high (my mom now demands I bring her back some every time I go). As for the croissants besides being absolutely delectable, they’re just humongous which is always very nice.

The atmosphere inside is very cozy with plenty of seating space and quite a variety of it as well. The area it’s located in is just a very cute neighborhood/Scenic area as well. The parking right next to the building, you do have to pay for it, but there is on street parking quite close!

Every time I’ve gone in the staff has always been very kind and lovely to me! Always being quite patient and amendable to answering questions.

Overall, this has to be one of my top, if not the top bakery  I’ve been to, in Austin. The pastries are SO yummy, and leave me craving going back again.

text.text:
My husband and I decided to try out Dai Due for our 8th anniversary, and unsurprisingly it was amazing! First off the reservations were pretty open mid-week; I had booked for Tuesday several weeks ahead of time but then had some plans shift and was able to change my reservation to Wednesday just a couple days ahead of time with no issues.

We walked in through the front as the back entrance wasn't really obvious from the parking lot (which is quite small), but that was cool as we got to walk by the deli counter and see the meat and pickled veggies etc that were for sale.  Our server was great, very helpful in suggesting items, explaining the menu, and answering any questions we had.

On her suggestion we started with the sauteed mushroom appetizer but also requested the black garlic butter to be added on the side (I don't think there was an up charge) and this was a great choice! The mushrooms were tender but with a nice bite and super flavorful. We also got the grilled oysters- I forgot exactly what was in the sauce it had miso and something else, but it was so rich and flavorful!  I couldn't decide what was the best between the two apps they were both amazing.

The husband ordered the antelope over regular fries (as he doesn't like sweet potatoes) which they were happy to accommodate.  It was delicious- tender and perfectly cooked with the chive butter on top. I had never had antelope before and found it very pleasant, not very gamey but with a slightly different flavor than beef.  I got the quail over grits with a creole sauce and sauteed kale- amazing! It comes with two quail that I think were spatchcocked- the only bones were in the legs and wings so you could eat it easily.  The grits were creamy and the sauce with the kale and quail was delicious.  I was able to finish my whole meal but was pretty stuffed at the end!

Our waitress encouraged us to get a dessert but when we declined brought us out a bowl of chai ice cream to share as she said she wasn't going to let us leave on our anniversary without a treat!

All in all a great experience, only complaints are that they don't serve cocktails (there are plenty of local Texas liquors to choose from!) but we did enjoy a glass of wine, and then went next door to Vic and Als after dinner for a dessert cocktail!

text.text:
We’ve been to Dish Society SEVERAL times now — for brunch, lunch, and happy hour — and every single visit always has some sort of hit!

The food here is fresh, local, and absolutely delicious, with so much care clearly put into every dish! The vibe inside is super cute, clean, and welcoming, with a small outdoor patio that’s perfect for a sunny Austin day and even if Austin's weird weather comes into play part of the outdoor seating is also covered.

When we've gone it’s never felt overly crowded (except one time during a morning rush, but we can see why) and the customer service has been phenomenal every time — from staff offering great recommendations to keeping tables spotless and making sure guests are happy.

We’ve loved everything we’ve tried, but a few standouts have been the Texas hot chicken sandwich (crispy, juicy, sweet, and savory perfection), the smoked salmon avocado toast (so fresh and flavorful), ranch-style eggs, and the grilled pesto chicken sandwich.

During happy hour, we grabbed the burger, some bites and drinks, with the burger for sure being a must — and the team even offered to cut the burger in half since we mentioned we were sharing. Small touches like that go a long way!

Their happy hour is also a great deal and definitely worth checking out. And if you’ve got a sweet tooth, don’t skip dessert — the Proud Pies they source from Houston are dangerously good. We still need to go back just to do a full pie tasting! The white chocolate pretzel bread pudding was warm, rich, and gave off total almond croissant vibes.

Oh, and don’t sleep on the mimosa flight — or their Mug Club, where you can purchase a YETI at their location and get free coffee refills when you bring it in. Genius!

All around, Dish Society is one of those rare spots that nails fresh, local food, great service, and good vibes every time. We highly recommend it! We'll be back, obviously!

-The French onion soup had excellent flavor and the bread and cheese were perfectly baked on top of the soup. Exactly what you imagine when you think of a perfect French onion.

-The fried shrimp po boy has excellent. The breading was delicious, and the sauce took it over the top.

-the burger and frites was the only thing that I felt was truly lacking. It was just a bit too simple for me for 20. Maybe I’m being a bit too harsh though as I had previously had the best burger in my life while in Chicago at Au Cheval.

Vibes: This restaurant has such a charm from its interior down to its quaint location. We dined outside, but the inside was very cozy as well.

Service: FoH is very generous and polite. Enjoyed my interactions with everyone.

text.text:
Our visit to Nomade Restaurant was nothing short of exceptional—a true winner from start to finish.

From the moment we walked in, everything felt thoughtfully curated. The ambience is warm and inviting, with lush green plants surrounding the tables and soft lighting that creates a relaxed, almost transportive vibe. What made it even more special was the energy of the staff—every server seemed genuinely happy to welcome and serve, which added such a personal touch to the experience.

One of the biggest highlights for us was the menu. My husband was thrilled to discover an entire vegan selection with so many options—it’s rare to see that level of care and variety. And the food? Absolutely outstanding. The coconut flatbread was truly to die for—easily one of the best dishes we’ve had in a while.

Every plate we ordered was beautifully presented and packed with flavor. You could taste the attention to detail in each bite, making the entire meal feel elevated yet comforting.

An unforgettable dining experience that checks every box—ambience, service, and incredible food. Already looking forward to going back.

text.text:
4 Stars – Beautiful Tulum Vibes with a Few Areas for Growth

We had a lovely evening at Nomadé and left feeling transported to the Yucatán with Tulum vibes — the jungle inspired design, open-fire kitchen, and tropical atmosphere are spot on. The food was mostly excellent, though a couple of small tweaks could take it to the next level.

The coconut crudo was exceptionally flavorful with a bold coconut presentation, though the portion was quite small. The Tempura Pescado Tacos were filling (three per order) and crunchy, but fairly mild — an optional salsa or spice would help. The Cochinita Pibil entree was the standout: tender, delicious, and full of authentic flavor.

Service was friendly but noticeably distant and a bit detached. Making a reservation was frustrating — they’re often “solidly booked” for 1–2 hours out, yet when you’re there you can see entire sections closed off. It’s hard to tell if it’s due to staffing or intentional scarcity to build hype. This felt especially surprising given how genuinely warm and welcoming the real hospitality is in Tulum and the Yucatán.

Overall, we’d rate the food 4/5, atmosphere 4/5, and service 4/5. Nomadé is def a strong recommendation for anyone craving that coastal Yucatecan escape in Austin — it just has a little room to grow in portion value, seasoning options, and that signature Mexican warmth.

Very, very interesting decor, done in sort of a Mediterranean style.   I liked it, but the club music playing in the background seemed inapproriate for the vibe. It is quite open with little, if any closed off areas. We went on a chilly morning, yet the heaters took away any hint of the cold.

The waitstaff was very friendly, casually dressed and took pains to say nice things to us upon our departure.

We went for breakfast and had a carafe of French Press coffee which was bold and very smooth, 2 Wagyu Tacos and a gluten free waffle. The torillas were small, but each had so much on them, I could only eat one and they gladly packed thge other to go. I wish I had noticed it came with pickled onions. Aside from that, I really enjoyed it. One reason we came here from North of Austin is they are entirely gluten-free and my wife thoroughly enjoyed her waffle. It is offered with a nice fruit variety, but we requested just the kiwi for dietary reasons.

Overall, it was a good experience.

Then the food came. It was genuinely one of the nastiest breakfasts I've ever had. I got the chicken and pancakes, and the chicken was just a tiny, tiny piece. My partner ordered a waffle and a chicken biscuit, and the biscuit was so dry with another minuscule piece of chicken. Honestly, I felt like I would've had a better, more worthwhile meal at Ihop.

text.text:
We came to Summer on Music Lane for a date night, something my wife and I haven’t done in at least a year. My mom was in town, so we jumped at the chance for a night out. Overall, the experience was really great.

We started with the Ora King Salmon Crudo. It was good. I love capers, which is why I ordered the dish. The onions bring a strong flavor while the pear is more subtle, which balances everything nicely.

For our mains, we ordered the Squid Ink Orecchiette and the 44 Farms Strip Steak, with the Sweet Potato Papas Bravas as a side to share.

The Squid Ink Orecchiette was excellent and had a nice kick to it. I would definitely order it again.

The 44 Farms Strip Steak was ordered medium rare and cooked perfectly. The flavor was great, and it was paired with dressed arugula, which really brightened the dish and made for a great combination.

The Sweet Potato Papas Bravas were excellent as well. Soft on the inside with a great texture, and the butter had a really nice spice flavor that tied the dish together.

Our server also recommended a bottle of Duo, which was a nice pairing with the meal.

Service was great and the food was great. The only reason this ends up being a 4/5 instead of a 5 is a small detail, but one that stood out. As you can see in the photo, we were given a standard glass carafe for water instead of the green-tinted fish carafes that other tables had. It made our table feel a little less special and a little less coordinated overall.

We did ask if we could get one, but were told they had unfortunately run out. It may simply be that there aren’t enough for every table.

Small detail overall, but one that stood out during an otherwise really nice meal.

October 2025

This was my first time at the Grove Wine Bar & Kitchen and always told it was excellent but with limited parking.  I arrived before the lunch crowd but was already packed and ended up getting the last spot in a tiny parking garage. I did notice a parking valet attendant but not sure where he parks the vehicles.

Walked through a courtyard with giant oak trees to get to the entrance and was quickly seated in the courtyard. It was a bit cold inside. Our server was really nice and helped me select a wine to pair with my meal.  I ordered the Avocado BLT. Eating outside felt special under the giant oak trees wrapped in tiny lights.

My order arrived and the BLT had hickory smoked bacon, smashed avocado, lettuce, tomato, red onion, garlic-herb aioli in a toasted sourdough. It also came with potato chips where should have substituted with a salad. The sandwich was really good and the ingredients tasted very fresh. Overall had great flavor. With this and the wine I had a very nice meal.

text.text:
I visited for brunch for the first time with a friend after seeing so many beautiful posts about it on Austin pages—I knew I had to check it out for myself.

When you arrive, there’s both street and lot parking (I chose street parking), and you walk up a gravel driveway to the restaurant. One of the most unique touches was the peacocks roaming the venue and nearby neighborhoods!

We came without a reservation, were seated at the bar, and only waited about 10–15 minutes for our table. The drink menu was a highlight for me…the presentation was stunning, and each drink was strong yet perfectly balanced.

Our server and the entire staff were exceptional, making sure everything from our water to our food and drinks was just right. The food came out quickly and was absolutely delicious. On a gloomy, overcast day, this turned out to be the perfect brunch spot.

I truly appreciated the wonderful experience. The venue is beautiful, the prices are reasonable, and the atmosphere is calm and inviting. Everything feels so thoughtfully curated, and I’d love to come back again especially for dinner.

text.text:
Electric Atmosphere & Family-Friendly Fun at Brazilian Carnaval!

I visited Ani’s Day & Night for the first time specifically for the Brazilian Carnaval celebration, and I absolutely loved it! I arrived extra early to secure a parking spot, which gave me a chance to soak in the very chill, laid-back morning vibe of the place before the party kicked off.

I ordered hot chocolate and tea, and both were surprisingly delicious and high-quality! The staff members were also incredibly friendly and welcoming. As a first-time spectator of Brazilian dancers, I was so excited by the performance—the energy was infectious! What I appreciated most was that the atmosphere was joyous and vibrant without being "wild." Earlier in the evening, I saw many parents with children, making it a great spot for both families and those looking to grab a drink.

The overall vibe is fantastic, and I will definitely be back for more events. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a unique Austin experience!

text.text:
Freddo’s ATX is an absolute gem, all year round! Whether it’s a sunny afternoon or a starry night. Though, I absolutely love their lights at night; they transform the space and it honestly feels like magic.

The atmosphere is relaxed yet lively, and the decor hits that perfect balance between modern and cozy. It’s a cute, inviting spot with plenty of space to hang—there’s indoor seating, a charming patio, and even an upstairs area if you’re looking for a quieter corner. In the colder months, the fireplace makes it extra cozy, and the staff are always kind, regularly adding wood to keep it warm and welcoming.

There’s live music happening all the time, which adds so much character and makes every visit feel special. The house itself is historic, and you can feel that charm in every detail.

The menu is just as impressive as the ambiance—fresh, creative options whether you’re craving a great coffee or something to eat. In a city full of great hangouts, Freddo’s ATX truly stands out as one of my favorite spots.

If you’re in the area, do yourself a favor and check it out—you won’t be disappointed!

Well well well….

I was a bit skeptical because the reviews are quite divided but let me tell you…go ahead and give this place a try. The biscuit sandwich was stellar, I LOVED the corn flavor that came through ever so slightly - don’t forget to try it with the hot sauce! The twinkies are nice IF you enjoy corn flavored desserts. They start off not too sweet but definitely get you on the backend after a second bite.

Customer service was pleasant! I was able to ask questions about the menu and didn’t feel like a menace lol.  It led me to trying the biscuit sando as I was told it was quite delicious. I’ll be back again. I can see why some wouldn’t like it - if you don’t like corn/masa in breads/pastries then maybe try a burrito. I’m always down to try modern twists on foods when it’s a merge of cultures.

Simple but effective and delicious menu. Not to mention I don’t feel like a glutton after eating the entire biscuit sando.

text.text: We have walked by this place dozens of times, but we never really thought to try it out until this morning. We entered the space, and we were offered menus as soon as we walked through the door. The variety of main dishes and sides was ample. We were originally on the hunt for a breakfast sandwich, and we found so much more. The space is large and bright, and pretty busy - but not overwhelmingly so. We ordered at the counter, and took a seat toward the back. Our party of four had no trouble finding a table. The food took about 10 minutes to arrive, and it looked good before it even got to the table. Thumbs up all around for the Lil Nasty breakfast sandwich, breakfast plate, and the Avacado BLT w/ egg on sour dough. The avacado was freshly sliced and generous, tomato was cool and crisp, stacked lettuce leaves gave the sandwich excellent texture, and the bacon was crisp and hearty. The was kind of an afterthought...I really enjoyed it. The Hangover Potato's were really great, not sure what they did in terms of preparation, but they were unique in taste and texture. Very good. Also, one of my sides was sliced strawberries. Normally a ho-hum side, but this place upped the ante by including chopped basil with the strawberries - game changer! The whole experience was great and definitely going back next time I'm in Austin. Our only bother was the volume level of the music...seemed a little loud, but the general clientele were probably on their 20s and 30s, so probably more to their liking. If you are comfortable with a slightly quirky menu, then go for it! You won't be disappointed.

text.text:
Prior to an event at the Long Center, we roamed across the river to the 2nd St District in sunny Austin for a bite.   My dinner choice of Gummie Bears at the Candy store was overruled...so we hit up Local Foods!  The vibe here is great with 2 levels of seating as well as outdoor and to go options.
Gal that took our order was efficient, friendly and helpful.  The Fall Dinner menu was exceptionally unique...I had the Gulf Seafood PoBoy with Apple/Cranberry salad and red potato salad for sides.   The potato salad is now my 2nd favorite, but will never surpass my #1 fave which is my dead Mom's specialty--just dont tell her!
The PoBoy was not the typical fake crab, small shrimp and an overload of mayo.  This was phenomenal.  The fresh dill in the potato salad took it up a notch.   My other half had a waygu beef sandwich with Mexican flavors.  Fantastic as well.  Too and we didnt save room for the brown butter miso cookies or carrot cake.   Great meal!  Now on to see Nick Offerman with a fully satisfied stomach......

I stopped at Knuckle Sandwich to pick up a couple of sammies for my friend and I.  We decided to go with the OG Knuckle Sandwich and the Mushroom Reuben.  I also got a side of the pickled beets.

The beets had a great pickled flavor, but they were much more crunchy than I expected.  I think my only recommendation for that would be to cook them a tad longer so they're a hair softer.  But otherwise, I would order them again.

The Mushroom Reuben was good.  I think I prefer classic Reubens haha, but this is a great option for all you vegetarians out there.

The Knuckle Sandwich is absolutely where it's at though.  Think an Italian sandwich with a Middle Eastern spin.  The za'atar vinaigrette added such an amazing flavor to a sandwich with fantastic bread, tasty meat, and a healthy amount of veggies.

I look forward to trying their other sandwiches as well as eating another Knuckle Sandwich.

I generally write in for their gluten free version, and happily wait the small amount of extra time it takes for Nick to make his magic happen.

text.text:
Nixta Taqueria was absolutely incredible! The farm-to-table concept, creative menu, and James Beard Award-winning chef make this place truly special.
We started with the chips and dip and the refried beans cooked in duck fat, which were unbelievably delicious. Then came the duck carnitas taco, and it was so good I literally said “fire” four times.
One of the best parts of the experience was having the chef personally deliver our food and take the time to chat with us. That level of warmth and hospitality made the meal even more memorable.
They offer both indoor and outdoor seating, and the pricing felt very fair for the quality and creativity of the food. Our server, Sam, was the icing on the cake. He was personable, knowledgeable, and made the entire experience even better.
Nixta Taqueria is a must-visit. Five stars without hesitation!

text.text:
I live in Austin and have wanted to try this place for a long time, the owners are famous for being part of a local "taco mafia" with some other local taco places.

It took a while to order and get seated, plan to wait if it's a Friday night.

The food was good, my table shared chips and 3 dips. Tasty but kinda small portion. I had the duck carnita, very filling and rich. That was enough food for me. The fermented pineapple drink was my favorite part of the meal. My partner had the carrot tostada which we were told was not that spicy, but guess what, it was so spicy that's all you could taste.
The milk rice pudding dessert was super disappointing, way too sweet, rice wasn't fully cooked and again small portion.

Regarding the atmosphere- the place is very cool and laid back, the garden is a great touch, most of the seating is picknik tables or chairs with no backs. To get a table with chairs we had to sit closer to the speakers and the noise was way too loud. We all had to yell over the music to have a conversation, not my thing.

Overall the food was good but overpriced. This is a place for young Gen Z's who love standing in line for food, uncomfortable seating and overpaying.

text.text:
If you want to eat inside, note that it’s by reservation only. They do have a large patio for walk-ins, but I recommend getting there early. We got there right after they opened at 5:00 pm and waited around 30 minutes to order. The patio is communal seating.

I liked the concept and the service was great, but the food that I tried wasn’t for me. I had one of their seasonal items, the blue crab tostada, which was good but the price was bit expensive for one tostada. I also had their barbacoa tacos, which were greasy, and the flavor of the lamb was strong. I wish they had disclosed that the meat was lamb and not beef. If I had known this, I wouldn’t have ordered them. Their menu is very limited, and I didn’t see any chicken or beef items.

My husband had the chorizo quesadilla and the duck carnitas taco, and he wasn’t impressed with either. He said the quesadilla was something you could easily make at home but nothing special. The duck carnitas taco was good, but he also felt it was a bit greasy.

We also didn’t like that they don’t give you the salsas on the side to add yourself, instead, the tacos already come dressed with salsa. This took away from the traditional experience of eating tacos.

Overall, I was very much looking forward to trying a Michelin rated restaurant, but I’m sad to say that I was disappointed. Again, they seem to have good quality ingredients, but it just wasn’t for me. Also, parking is difficult.

text.text:
There is a good amount of hype behind Asado’s so we expected some pretty good food going into it and what we got was something close but just a bit short. The lot Asado’s is in is nice with covered seating and other food trucks all around. They were pretty busy for a drizzly Saturday afternoon so ordering ahead was a good call for us. The food took probably 30 minutes or so between ordering to receiving the text it was really to pickup. They don’t have a pickup window as far as we could see so we waited on line and then grabbed our food at the front.

The food itself was good but not nearly what was expected in relation to its hype, something that feels a bit common in Austin. We ordered a carnitas super burrito and a cheese quesadilla. The super burrito came with the wrong meat, instead coming with chicken that had a bit of a dry and burnt flavor in it. Luckily that was masked by the rest of the burrito which did taste pretty good. The tortilla itself was soft but with a little bit of crisp to it that gave it a nice bite. Unfortunately, the cheese quesadilla was a miss. The tortilla on it was burnt and very crispy, which some may like, but is definitely not our preference. For what it’s worth, maybe this is just a style of Mexican food we don’t prefer but either way if you fall in line with that kind of flavor profile then maybe have a bit more realistic expectations coming into this place. Again, Asado’s is not bad, just not great. We’d suggest going for yourself and seeing if you’d agree.

I’m from the San Francisco Bay Area and there’s nothing like a Mission burrito. Just like there is nothing like Texas BBQ. So, I am always very leery of reviews that reference  “mission burrito”, but also hopeful. With that said, although not a Mission burrito, I was, very pleasantly surprised and it was 100% worth the drive across town. Everyone seems to be hyping the steak super burrito. I tried both the steak and  chicken super burrito and I actually liked the chicken better.
I don’t think you can go wrong with either one though. I’d eat either one again and again.

Food truck, but they have picnic tables, misters and umbrellas , so you can eat it there comfortably.

text.text:
I ordered the Super Burrito with steak (crispy), a Super Taco with carnitas, and chips with salsa. Overall, I thought the portions were generous and the prices were fair, especially for freshly made food.

As for the flavor, I would not call it bland like some other reviews have mentioned, although taste is obviously subjective. To me, the food leaned more on the mild side rather than being heavily seasoned. It was still enjoyable, but I do think the steak and carnitas could use a little more depth and boldness in flavor.

One thing that really stood out was the service. The ladies working there were incredibly friendly and welcoming, which made the whole experience even better. The food truck itself, along with the seating area, had a very warm, family-friendly vibe that made it a pleasant place to eat.

There was a bit of a wait, but it felt worth it because the food was made fresh. That said, if you are in a hurry, I would definitely recommend placing an online pickup order ahead of time.

I’d give this place 4.5 stars. The only reason I’m taking off half a star is because the meat portions felt a little lighter than I would have liked, and the steak and carnitas were somewhat too mild for my taste. I completely understand the realities of inflation and rising costs, but I’d honestly rather see a small price increase than a reduced meat portion. The food is still good, and I think customers would keep coming back.

text.text:
🌮 I Took One Bite… Then Walked Straight to the Chef to Say Thank You.

When a local tells you, “You HAVE to try this taco spot,” you listen. While exploring Austin, we received a recommendation for Discada, and this was one of those food experiences where the hype was absolutely justified.

The biggest surprise? It’s not a traditional sit-down restaurant—it’s a food truck. But don’t let the humble setup fool you. This little truck has earned national attention, including recognition in the MICHELIN Guide Texas for its unique approach to Mexican cuisine.

After my first bite of their signature discada taco, I literally wanted to find the chef and compliment them. That’s how memorable it was.

🔥 What Makes Discada Special?

Before visiting, I had never tried discada tacos.

Discada is a traditional Northern Mexican cooking style where different cuts of meat are cooked together on a large metal cooking disc (“disco”), creating layers of flavor as the ingredients slowly combine.

At Discada, this concept is taken seriously. Their signature mixture combines beef and pork with ingredients like bacon, onion, roasted poblano peppers, and aromatic seasonings, then serves it taco-style with fresh toppings and salsa.

The result?

A taco that is smoky, savory, juicy, and completely different from your typical taco experience.

🌮 The Must-Try: Discada Tacos

This was my first time trying discada tacos, and honestly, I wondered why I waited so long.

The meat had:

* Incredible depth of flavor
* Tender texture
* A perfect balance of richness and freshness
* Just enough toppings to enhance the taco without covering up the star ingredient

Every bite had something happening—savory meat, fresh toppings, and layers of seasoning that kept me coming back for another bite.

🚚 The Food Truck Experience

One of the things I love about Austin’s food scene is that some of the most memorable meals come from unexpected places.

Discada proves that a food truck can deliver a world-class experience.

No fancy dining room. No unnecessary extras.

Just a focused menu, passionate cooking, and one specialty done exceptionally well.

💡 Tips for First-Time Visitors

* Come hungry—the menu is intentionally focused around their signature discada tacos—they are small but mighty in flavor!
* Trust the specialty. This is not the place to play it safe with a standard taco order.
* Expect a casual outdoor food truck experience, but stay for the incredible flavors.
* Go with friends so you can enjoy the full experience together.
* Don’t forget to squeeze the lime it enhances the flavor.
* Get the ELOTE EN VASO—corn so tasty.

Austin has no shortage of amazing taco spots, but Discada stands out because it celebrates a lesser-known Mexican tradition and turns it into something unforgettable.

Sometimes the best restaurants aren’t the biggest or fanciest. Sometimes they are a small food truck with a big passion for one incredible dish.

When one taco is good enough to make you stop eating and go thank the chef… you know you’ve discovered something special. 🤩🙏🏻😋

So Discada is among the "four horsemen" of the Austin taco scene as I've heard it called (though no one can fully agree on the four), and I'll start by saying that it is a step above most in terms of flavor. They have one option (discada) with 5 meats, pineapple, onions, and various spices. The taste and texture is on point, meaty and rich, though it's pretty damn greasy compared to most. The elote en vase I actually liked more, and given the size of the tacos, I definitely needed it. Both salsas were great, though I preferred the poblano.

Look, I can't sugarcoat it, $8.50 for 3 tacos that are about the size of one $3 Joe's bakery taco is a bit nuts. I can cook good food, I don't generally go to restaurants for value alone, but then Cuantos tacos basically beat this on all points (and you can choose your meats). Paprika similarly beats this. Taqueria 10/10. Las Trancas. Taqueria Ensenada or Marisco for seafood. It's not bad, it's just the worst of the hyped taco places, and I can't see myself coming back.

text.text:
Veracruz Fonda Bar was unbelievably good! Prices may seem a bit steep but given the quality and frankly quantity of food we got it was well worth it!

We started with an agua Fresca de limón, a freshly squeezed limeade that was delicious, even while partially frozen it never tasted watered down or diluted.

I ordered the birria taco platter, and this is my favorite Quesabirria platter I’ve had in all of Texas! It’s lamb/beef mix that feels lighter on your stomach than regular lamb birria and it was DELICIOUS! You get two tacos with the platter but you get served heartily, and it comes with a bed of rice, your side of consomé with hominy, a spicy green chile based salsa with a kick, some garnishes and onions for the quesabirria tacos, a flame grilled pepper, and a wedge of lime for good measure. It’s a must have for sure!! If you’re wondering whether or not you’ll be full after, order it, and see how you feel before ordering more food.

My wife got the 2 taco platter, and you can mix and match which tacos you get. She got the shrimp taco with a chicken milanesa tacos. That came with a side of rice, a side of beans, and a green chile based salsa with a nice kick.

As a sweet treat my wife ordered the fried plantains, and they were perfect, not too sweet, just right.

Our server was incredible, though we didn’t get his name, but the service was outstanding. We will definitely be back! If you’re in the area, definitely check this place out!

text.text:
Lil' Easy’s on Cesar Chavez has a rustic, old-school Louisiana, hole-in-the-wall vibe that makes the experience feel authentic from the moment you walk in.

We started with the red beans and rice, and it immediately landed in my top five of all time. It was fresh, flavorful, and had all the right authentic Louisiana taste. My wife had the gumbo and said it ranked among her top ten gumbos ever.

The prime rib po’boy was delicious. Next time, I’ll get mayonnaise instead of horseradish, but it was still a great sandwich. We also tried the catfish basket with potato salad and the chicken tender basket with fries. Everything came out fresh and hot, and the fries were especially good.

The customer service was great, and the entire experience was enjoyable. This was an ideal spot for good Louisiana-style food, and we will definitely be returning.

A strong 4-star experience for me. Five stars are reserved for food that makes me cry!

text.text:
I’ve been on the hunt for my New Orleans flavors right here in Austin, and thanks to the Frankie App, I stumbled across this spot and thought, “Why not go see?” Baby, I was not ready. I walked in and instantly felt like I’d stepped straight into the Bayou. The vibe hits you before you even sit down.

They greeted us at the door, and we barely waited to be seated. Indoor and outdoor seating are both available, and inside is spaced out just right—close enough to feel the energy, but not so close you’re sharing conversations with strangers. Menus are available by QR code or paper, whichever you prefer.

Our server, Claire, was a whole experience by herself—genuine, funny, honest, and fast. We ordered drinks (yes, Bourbon Street‑style and strong in all the right ways), and by the time I stood up to grab my glasses, those beauties were already on the table. Service here does not play.

The hardest part of the entire visit? Deciding what to order. The menu is stacked from top to bottom—drinks, appetizers, entrées, desserts, all of it.

We started with the Deviled Eggs and the Boudin Balls. Listen… there are no human words for how perfect those Boudin Balls were. Hot, crispy, flavorful—10/10. And if you dip them in that sauce, it takes them straight to an 11. The deviled eggs were creamy, savory, and topped with bacon—little pockets of joy.

For entrées, we had the Catfish Atchafalaya (a run‑don’t‑walk situation). I don’t even eat catfish, and I was tearing this dish up. I ordered the Chicken & Andouille Sausage Jambalaya, and baby, it had me dancing in my seat.

We wrapped it all up with their Gas Station Beignets. I told Claire whoever is back there making these must’ve gotten the recipe from Café Du Monde because they taste exactly the same. I’m honestly shocked there isn’t a line wrapped around the block for these alone.

This place is a 100/100 for me. If you love authentic Cajun cuisine, this is a must‑try. Austin, we’ve got a little slice of New Orleans hiding right here on East Ceasar Chavez.
