First time going to La Volta Pizza club was a success. Well, the second time. Don't make the mistake of going here on a busy weekend night without a reservation. It's going to take a while to get sat, which after eating here, I can see why this is a small little pizza shop. It doesn't have a lot of capacity. Came back on a Monday night with the reservation and it was smooth sailing.
Started off with an order of the meatballs. Amazing, great rich meatballs with a perfect sauce to balance it out. Then decide to share the hot girl pasta with the table. I will say this rigatoni alla vodka with sausage was a little bit spicy but we aren't the biggest spice people. Still it was delicious. Then the vodka pizza came out. We were a little scared that the vodka on the pizza would be just as spicy. It really didn't seem to be, the cheese balanced the vodka sauce very well and you couldn't notice the spice anymore. The crust on these pizzas is phenomenal. I think some of the best in Austin. Next we ordered the classic pie with extra sauce. That was a great and subtle difference compared to the vodka pie. Again, another all around amazing pizza. These pies are pretty dang big, you could definitely share one with three to four people. But there's no problem with leftover pizza for me. Great work guys

text.text:
I’m from Vancouver and aburi oshi is a massive thing over there. It’s become popular among other big Canadian cities and I’m so freaking glad it has made its way to Austin :)!

The sushi scene in Vancouver is pretty big so let me know tell you this. Please ignore all the bad reviews Aburi oshi has gotten on Google so far. I see people upset about the wait but hell, it’s a soft opening and they’re trying to figure it out. I see people complaining that it’s just not good and hell, they probably don’t know good sushi lol.

The recipe, quality, and taste is the exact same that you’d get at Miku in Vancouver. I’ve ordered from their ghost kitchen multiple times and it has been consistent and tasty each time. My favorite is the salmon and ebi oshi sushi.

This has always been the one unique sushi dish I make all my American friends try when they visit Vancouver and they’ve always loved it. Excited for when they finally open an official location and expand further :)!

text.text:
Food was okay but nothing special. Pretty bummed because it was a prix fixe menu of what should have been their greatest hits.

I felt like the panisse needed some sort of sauce since it was a bit dry by itself. The cantaloupe gazpacho tasted unusual. The balance of the beef tartare was off and the flavor of the meat is overshadowed by all of its other components. The steak was chewy and the sauce was way too sweet.   The veggies accompanying it also needed more acidity as it was on the blander side.

I did like the pasta, the focaccia, and the cornbread, though simpler and more basic.

I’d like to believe that their true greatest hits lie every other night when they are on their regularly scheduled program. But since I also hated their queue system, it might be a while since I come back to find out.

text.text: Birdie’s is absolutely delicious and well worth the wait! They do have limited reservations on OpenTable, but otherwise they take walk-ins, but you can expect a line. When we didn’t have a reservation, we waited over an hour and a half, but the experience made the wait enjoyable. You can order wine or beer while you wait, and the vibrant atmosphere helps the time fly by. It’s a fixed menu where you get multiple appetizers, then choose one main and one dessert. We also went during one of their Italian-themed months, and some of my favorites were the mozzarella sticks, cacio e pepe, and the soft serve ice cream. You can also order a bottle of wine, and if you don’t finish it, they’ll reseal it so you can take the rest home. The staff have chill personalities but are very attentive and genuine. Can’t recommend enough. One of our favorite spots in Austin!

Different like the fablemans you might say. That film wasn’t for everyone. And maybe birdies isn’t either. But it’s still speilberg. It still hits. These pastas are incredible.

text.text: So delicious, flavorful and rich!  I was blown away going to Paprika ATX for the first time.  I went with my wife and we decided to split 5 quesitacos between the two of us.  We had the suadero, carnitas, tinga de pollo, nopalitos and champinones.  First, I love the layer of griddled cheese to the tacos.  It definitely enhances it and takes it to another level.  Second, I love the wide array of sauces to choose from.  Beware of the rojo sauce.  I enjoyed it because I like it spicy.  But my wife struggled a bit LOL.  The verde sauce was more her speed.  Third, the food comes out very fast.  Fourth, the staff were extremely friendly.  Fifth, we enjoyed the music, vibes and ambiance inside.  Sixth, they had some interesting flavors of Agua Fresca that I never tried before, which were tasty and refreshing.  Lastly, the food was unbelievable.  We only tried the quesitacos but were already planning to come back to try the quesadillas and tortas.  I’d say this is a must try in Austin!

I tried the Smoked Red Fish Toast from the brunch menu, and it was one of my favorite dishes. The smoked fish was fresh, flavorful, and not fishy at all. It was topped with onions, radish, dill, chives, a squeeze of lemon, and salsa verde, which made every bite bright, refreshing, and well-balanced.

The sourdough toast was also excellent—crispy on the outside, chewy on the inside, and sturdy enough to hold all the toppings without getting soggy. The combination of smoky fish, fresh herbs, tangy lemon, and crunchy vegetables was delicious. If you’re looking for a light but satisfying brunch, I’d definitely recommend this dish.

TL;DR: I went at happy hour and indeed was quite happy with everything! $6 burger, $6 drinks, good vibes. Will come back.

Food:
I went during happy hour, and I ordered a smash burger ($6), a paloma ($6), and an aperol spritz ($8). The burger is nothing extraordinary (just a patty and cheese), but it has a good flavor to it and is not greasy. I would totally order the paloma again: it has a nice subtle grapefruit flavor to it. Aperol spritz is a classic, but I would rather order another paloma!

Service:
You just scan a QR code to order, and you can open/close a tab easily. Love that it accepts Apple pay. Food came like 15 minutes before my drinks did, so there is definitely a bit of wait with drinks.

Ambiance:
I love the vibe out here -- it is essentially just a ton of benches with umbrellas to vibe at. A very chill outdoor experience, and all of my friends had positive things to say as well :)

text.text:
Overall Experience: This place truly exceeded expectations! The ambiance was warm and inviting, creating a perfect atmosphere for a great dining experience. The service was exceptional, with attentive staff making sure every detail was taken care of.

Starters: I began with the Duck Fat Fries—while they were solid and well-prepared, they didn’t quite stand out as much as I’d hoped. On the other hand, the Bone Marrow was an absolute highlight! Rich and flavorful, it paired beautifully with the fries, creating a satisfying combination that elevated the overall experience.

text.text:
We went to Salty Sow on a Friday evening. We had a reservation and were promptly sat outside. They have huge fans, so in spite of the heat it was very pleasant.

We were excited to try the food, and were hungry. Our server appeared (I can't remember his name but he was a short guy with blond hair). I ordered a cocktail and my husband ordered beer to begin with. He went away and then came back asking my husband if he wanted some whiskey cocktail, and we corrected him that we had asked for a particular beer. No big deal.

We then ordered the deviled eggs and shishito peppers, and the red fish and short ribs for entree. A lady brought us the drinks, and the deviled eggs. Our server swung by and then disappeared. We thought the shishito peppers were on their way. We waited  for what seemed like a really long time and still no shishito peppers. We also noticed that each table had a carafe of water except ours. We were just given water once, and then our server never bothered to fill the water up. Anyway, we kept waiting since there was no sign of the server. At this point, we felt he might have forgotten the second appetizer and we just did not want it, but he was nowhere to be found. A man (not our server) brought out our entrees. We then told him that we had been waiting for our second appetizer and would just want to cancel it. We asked if we could get the biscuits instead. He brought out the biscuits within a few minutes.

Now this is where it really annoyed us. Had our server just come over and said he had forgotten our shishito peppers, it would have been okay. Human. What he tried was act smart and dropped by saying the shishito peppers would be out to which we said that we didn't want an appetizer after an entree and had cancelled it. I almost felt like he was treating us as if he thought we don't really dine out or whatever and he could just make fools of us. This really didn't sit right with me. We asked him for water and he filled it up left.

The food was above average. The short ribs were good but my red fish had been hammered! The biscuits were good. The deviled eggs were good as well. Anyway, we finished our meal, and got the check, paid, and were waiting to finish our drinks. The receipt was on our table. Also, note, it was not a particularly busy day with several empty tables. What our server did next was absolutely unacceptable. I think he wanted to see if we had tipped him after his awful service. We did, but not 20% as we always do because of the soddy job he did, not to mention his attitude. We paid 15% which I think was more than what he deserved now. Out of nowhere, and mind you,after being absent for long periods before, he just came by, grabbed the paid up bill from our table to our shock, while we were still sitting and talking, looked at the bill, turned towards us, and muttered something angry under his breath and walked away. I have never seen this level of entitlement and bad behavior.

We left right away. We had been really looking forward to this meal but I would not want to go back. The food was good, but not great, and I would not want to put up with such obnoxious behavior as a paying customer.

text.text:
Overall, we really enjoyed our experience here. The pizza slices were huge but they were light, crispy, and cooked to order so it's very fresh. If you want to have a bit more flavor, it's best to order a side of chili oil or ranch to dip your pizza in.

We came on a Saturday night during July 4 for a quick dinner before seeing the fireworks and it was a very great meal. There was a line trailing outside the door but the wait wasn't bad. We were offered the menu and drinks while we waited, and there were some seats available. Since we came when the sun was setting, it wasn't too hot but there was a lot of little bugs that were biting our legs, so I would recommend some sort of bug spray or long pants.

The indoor dining was not big and had a few tables but there was a lot of take out orders and were constantly being rotated so we didn't have any wait after placing our order. They were really efficient in cleaning their tables and having them ready for the next guest. Even though we ordered and paid at the counter, they guided us to our table and serviced us like a restaurant. The staff were super friendly, easy to talk to, and had exceptional service.

We wanted to try a little bit of everything so we ordered per slice. We got 2 slices of the Spicy Margh, Sweet Sausage, Stracciatella, Pepperoni, and Pickle.

I love pickles so I was super excited to try out the pickle pizza, especially since I've seen it being advertised all over social media. I was afraid it was going to be overly wet and soggy from the juice, but it wasn't. The crust is super crispy and thin; the pickles were less sour than I expected and a bit crunchy. The cheese is creamy but didn't have much flavor. It came with a side of ranch dipping sauce but I preferred it without. It only had a bit of a pickle aftertaste, so if you're not into pickles but into crunchy, it's not a bad choice.

The spicy margh was okay. It had a bit of a spicy kick but it was only here and there. The menu said it had a tajin crust but it was their regular crust with a light sprinkle of tajin, which was not evenly distributed. We were thinking maybe because of that, the pizza was only spicy in a few spots. The cheese was really good though.

The sweet sausage was super sweet. I personally am not a fan of sweetness in my savory foods but my friend loved it. If you're into meaty, sweet, and savory profiles like BBQ, this may be it for you.

For the Stracciatella, we thought the white balls on top were going to be cheesy but it tasted and had the texture of yogurt. It made the pizza creamy but it didn't have much flavor to it. The tomato sauce was okay.

They did not skimp on the pepperoni. The pizza was good, though the pepperoni were the cup ones so it held on to more grease than the other slices. It was a bit more salty without being overbearing and very crispy.

I came here with my work, and it’s not really the type of restaurant I would normally choose. I tend to prefer Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, or Asian food. That said, they are clearly trying to provide a very good experience, and the location is really nice.

It was my first time trying crab cakes, and they were genuinely very good. The burger was good, and the fries came out extremely fresh and hot. No complaints there.

The atmosphere is a little more attentive and formal than I personally prefer. I’m more of a relaxed, leave-me-alone-with-my-food kind of person, but if you like attentive service and having your water glass constantly refilled, they were very good at it.

It was not too loud at all so in that sense a great place if you need to talk without yelling over music or other people.

I tried the tart that my friend got and in my opinion it was way to sweet. I usually find everything too sweet in the US so maybe other people like.

Overall, not necessarily my style of restaurant, but they did what they do very well.

text.text:
We’ve eaten brunch here 3x now and it’s one of our favorite spots in Austin! Super cute inside and out with excellent service from the bar tenders to servers to chef. We’ve sat at the bar on one occasion, inside table another and outside (in the shade) and all have been great. Highly recommend reservations as it’s been busy every time we’ve been here.

I also appreciate that there’s onsite parking (free) and even though the main lot is often full, there’s extra spaces by the shops next door (all part of the same complex).

Now, onto the food… we’ve sampled a lot and the fall burrata is my fave. The avocado toast, migas, artichoke, and charcuterie board are also excellent. And of course, the pastries and chocolate chip cookies are a must try every time you come! Overall, prices are fair and portions are generous, we leave happy and full every time.

Highly recommend trying this spot out for a brunch date, girls get-together or even an adult birthday meal. If you have to wait for a table, go next door to Tiny’s milk and cookies and grab coffee and treats while you wait. Enjoy!

text.text:
We had such a lovely time creating balloon décor for a birthday celebration at Tiny Boxwoods. We designed custom free-standing arches and lush organic garlands that perfectly complemented the restaurant’s charming garden-style atmosphere.

Tiny Boxwoods is already such a beautiful and intimate space, and it was the perfect backdrop for a joyful and stylish celebration. The combination of great energy, a warm setting, and thoughtful details made this event truly special.

We’re always grateful to be trusted with these meaningful moments and loved helping bring this birthday vision to life in such a stunning venue!

text.text: We love Lin and Qi is a solid choice when downtown or you can't find parking at Lin. The service is friendly and organized. The interior design is well thought out. The free parking is an ultimate plus, especially downtown.  Their wine selection and cocktails are top notch.  We came here for lunch on Saturday afternoon and enjoyed a special meal to celebrate the weekend.  We each ordered a soup: Hot and Sour as well as the Egg Drop with lump crab. Both were delicious. Then we shared a variety of small plates, including the shrimp-stuffed eggplant. These were so good that we ordered a second serving. We of course had the Pea shoots (an absolute must-have everytime), as well as the Salt and Pepper Shrimp, which were delicious and spiced just right. We will definitely come back again and again.

Delicious food Everytime. Service, however, is hit or miss apparently. Brought my Mom and daughter for their first time for lunar new year. We had mediocre service, less experience based than my first two visits, with little to no conversation or recommendations. We were the only table they dropped to-go boxes for, every other table they boxed their food for them, which was what happened my first two times. Makes it feel less of an experience than normal. They also gave us a desert menu that had 10 ish options and only 2 or 3 were available, which wasn't shared when we asked about desert but only when we were ready to order.
Beautiful decorations, louder than normal based on the new year but nothing terrible. akaushi beef, moo shu pork, and salt and epper shrimp all phenomenal. The soup dumplings never disappoint so that's always our first bite. Cocktails took some time but we're always delicious. We will probably be back but might take some time to forget the sun par service.

Visited Elizabeth Street Café with a friend and had a really nice experience. The place itself is beautiful and cozy, and the staff was polite and welcoming, which made the visit even more enjoyable.

We ordered the Ginger-Chili Oil Dumplings, Spicy Chicken Crunch Spring Rolls, Mushroom & Tofu Bun, and Chicken Banh Mi. The Chicken Banh Mi and the Dumplings were absolutely amazing and full of flavor — easily the highlights of the meal. The Spring Rolls and Mushroom & Tofu Bun were decent but felt more on the average side compared to the standout dishes.

We also tried their French Toast, and it was excellent — perfectly cooked, flavorful, and definitely something I’d recommend trying.

Overall, Elizabeth Street Café offers a great combination of good food, pleasant ambience, and friendly service. I’d happily come back again, especially for the Banh Mi, Dumplings, and French Toast.

Must-try: Chicken Banh Mi, Ginger-Chili Oil Dumplings & French Toast

I stopped in for dinner today and ordered the fried shrimp bahn mi, and it completely blew me away. The shrimp was perfectly crispy on the outside, juicy and flavorful inside, with just the right amount of heat. The veggies, fresh herbs, and house-made mayo came together in the most delicious way on that soft, lightly toasted baguette. Every bite was an explosion of texture and flavor.
My waitress, Cassidy, was an absolute rockstar. She was super friendly, attentive, and genuinely enthusiastic about the menu. She gave great recommendations and checked on us at the perfect times without being overbearing. Her warm service made the whole meal feel extra special.
The vibe of the restaurant is charming and welcoming too. I’ll definitely be back soon — this place is a hidden gem! Highly recommend the fried shrimp bahn mi and asking for Cassidy if she’s working. 10/10!
Thank you Elizabeth Street Cafe and Cassidy! 🙌

text.text:
Elizabeth Street Cafe on South Lamar in Austin is a culinary delight, masterfully blending the sophistication of French cuisine with the bold flavors of Vietnamese heritage. The ambiance echoes this fusion, creating a unique and captivating atmosphere.

The Vietnamese wonton soup, a creative reinterpretation of the classic French onion soup, was a highlight of our visit. Rich, comforting, and perfectly suited to a chilly evening, it showcased the cafe's ability to reimagine familiar dishes with unexpected flair.

The Bahn Coun was a testament to the kitchen's skill, with tender, expertly cooked meat and a harmonious balance of textures and flavors. Each component was carefully crafted to elevate the dish as a whole.

Dessert was a symphony of refined indulgence: the macarons were delicate, nuanced confections, while the chocolate sesame puff was a sublime marriage of crispy, nutty, and rich elements, a true tour de force of textural contrast and flavor pairing.

Overall, Elizabeth Street Cafe delivers a distinctive and captivating dining experience, one that will appeal to adventurous palaters and those seeking a sophisticated take on traditional flavors.

Chapulín Cantina is an absolute gem! Our recent visit was nothing short of exceptional, thanks in large part to our incredible waitress, Elizabeth. She was truly outstanding - attentive, engaging, and incredibly knowledgeable about the menu. Elizabeth's service alone puts her in my top 5 waitstaff experiences ever.

Don't miss out on their spicy margaritas - they were a hit at our table and complemented the food beautifully. The blend of flavors in both the food and drinks showed the kitchen's skill and attention to detail.
The atmosphere was vibrant and welcoming, making for a memorable dining experience. Chapulín Cantina offers a perfect blend of excellent service, outstanding food, and a great ambiance. It's definitely a must-visit spot in Austin for anyone looking for top-notch Mexican cuisine. We'll certainly be back!

text.text: This place far exceeded my expectations! Delicious food. Cool atmosphere. Elevated experience. I loved it! Came for late lunch just before happy hour and my server Joe was wonderful! I really appreciate the care he took with bringing me my food and making sure I was all set. The lemonade is fresh and so tasty—served in a sugar-rimmed glass. The wagyu tacos were fantastic, they look small but it was definitely plenty of food to be full on. Reminds me of a Barbacoa taco but less greasy and more delicious. The mole or salsa they bring with the chips at first is really tasty. Green one is spicy if you like spicy go for it! I mentioned that I was celebrating something and after my meal he brought me a slice of Tres Leches cake that was incredible! Excellent service, delicious food and a truly fun and unique experience. I love the decor like a fancy or elevated Low Rider theme and a perfect homage to Oaxaca, Mexico 🇲🇽 ❤️thank you for a wonderful and unique dining experience. It’s fun to people-watch in South Congress too. Plenty of parking in the lot or alongside the street.

This has been one of my best discoveries in the city of Austin, TX during the SXSW25. It's a very chill place, in a quiet corner just behind the street with all the music venues. The guys working here are funny and kind and food is great!
I had the Pork Bento Box and everything I ate was healthy yet very tasty. Prices are good too, a Bento box is 14$ and I think it is the highest price you can pay, and you get a Miso soup for free. My friend took a Shitake Tofu Bowl and it costs even less (it looked great as well, by the way).
I also loved the message you can read at the entrance.
A must visit in Austin, especially (but not only) if you love asian food.

text.text: Koriente offers a hearty meal with good portions at a reasonable price. The service is friendly, and they provide vegan options, which is a plus for those seeking plant-based meals. The food is healthy, though it lacks the robust flavor I was hoping for, possibly due to the focus on healthier ingredients. For example, the vegan miso soup didn't have enough salt for my taste, and the kimchi was a little bland. Overall, it's a decent spot for a wholesome meal without breaking the bank.

The restaurant is very simple and small but cute. There is patio seating in the back which allows dogs. You place your order at the counter and then your order will be brought to your table. There is free, vegan miso soup, which you could try (we did try it and found it to be OK? It was not very flavorful, but it had tiny tofu chunks in it). I got the tofu shiitake bowl and enjoyed it - it was a little spicy (in a good flavorful way). I got a side of the sesame, sweet potato noodles and really enjoyed it.
My friend got the spicy chicken bowl, but did not enjoy it much and it was not spicy either. My friend also got the kimchi and said it tasted very authentic.
If you dine while seated on the back porch, you might see cute Uber Eats robots around for delivery pick up.

One of my favorite restaurants from this trip to Austin!

From the moment we walked in, the staff was friendly, welcoming, and attentive. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, making for a great dining experience.

We started with the Burrata Caprese and the complimentary focaccia, both of which were excellent. For our mains, we had the Chicken Parmesan and the Gnochetti with creamy avocado pesto and added shrimp—everything was flavorful, well-balanced, and cooked perfectly. To finish, we enjoyed the Tiramisu, which was the perfect dessert to end the meal.

Every dish we tried was delicious, and the service made the experience even better. We will definitely be back the next time we’re in Austin!

text.text:
There are moments in life when you take one bite… stop chewing… look around the table… and quietly whisper, “Houston, we have a new champion.”

Ladies and gentlemen… I have officially found THE BEST Orange Chicken in Austin. 🏆🍊🐔

I’m not talking “pretty good.” I’m talking cancel your usual Chinese takeout order good.

The chicken stayed unbelievably crispy under that glossy, sweet, tangy, slightly spicy sauce. Every bite had that perfect crunch before exploding with flavor. It was the kind of dish where I kept saying, “One more piece…” about 17 times.

And don’t sleep on everything else either. The vegetable lo mein was fresh, loaded with veggies, and cooked perfectly. The egg rolls were golden, crispy, and exactly what you want to kick off the meal. Even the egg drop soup came out comforting and silky smooth—the perfect warm-up before the main event.

But what really made this place special? The atmosphere.

The dining room was absolutely buzzing. Tables full of families, friends sharing dishes, laughter echoing across the restaurant… it felt like the kind of neighborhood spot where memories are made just as much as meals. That’s exactly what Seat At The Table is all about.

Some restaurants serve dinner.

House of Three Gorges serves happiness by the plate.

💎 10 💎

This one earns the diamond. If you’re chasing the best Orange Chicken in Austin, the search is officially over. Save yourself a seat… and make sure someone orders the Orange Chicken, because fighting over the last piece is practically guaranteed. 🍊🥢🔥.

text.text:
House of Three Gorges is an absolute gem for anyone who truly appreciates authentic Sichuan cuisine. Sichuan flavors have a distinctive charm—bold, aromatic, layered with heat, and deeply satisfying—and this place delivers that experience beautifully every single time. As someone who is a big fan of Sichuan-style food, I’m always looking for restaurants that stay true to the cuisine rather than watering it down, and this spot does exactly that.
My buddies and I recently visited and shared several dishes, including the cumin lamb and the jumping fish, Sichuan dry fried chicken.. and all were outstanding. The cumin lamb was perfectly seasoned, tender, and packed with that signature smoky spice profile, while the jumping fish brought the classic numbing heat and complex flavors that Sichuan lovers crave. You can immediately tell the kitchen prioritizes authenticity and consistency—two things that keep us coming back.
The restaurant has built a strong reputation for delivering traditional flavors without compromise, and after multiple visits, I can confidently say the taste remains reliably excellent. If you enjoy real Sichuan cooking with depth, spice, and character, House of Three Gorges should absolutely be on your list.

Komé is good but could be great. The huge menu is a catch all of everything you could expect from Japanese cuisine. It's almost so much that there are too many options. Thankfully, most a very good choices!

The fries are great. It's weird to start with that but they really are. Same goes for pretty much any sushi. You'll be able to taste the freshness of the fish. However, avoid the curry and katsu. My katsu can only be described as overdone. The breading tasted nearly burnt dry and banding in the meat (see my photo) shows how it was separating from being cooked too long. The curry is as disappointing as their sister restaurant. It's weak enough that I'd venture I could produce a better curry in bulk.

So do come here and enjoy the sushi, but don't venture into the other menu items. They'd really shine by focusing on a core menu with less accompanying dishes.

text.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

My wife and I went to Kome last week and had an absolutely excellent sushi dinner. We arrived right when they opened and were able to grab a table for two — which worked out perfectly because this place fills up FAST. If you’re planning to visit, I highly recommend making a reservation or arriving early like we did.

The moment you walk into this charming sushi restaurant, you feel transported into a cozy little spot you’d imagine finding in Japan. One of the most memorable details is the collection of colorful waving lucky cats throughout the restaurant. They add such a fun, welcoming energy and pops of cheerful color everywhere you look.

The open sushi counter makes the experience even better. Watching the chefs carefully craft each roll and plate adds to the atmosphere and anticipation of the meal itself.

Must-order items:
• Karaage chicken
• French fries—yes, really, you’ll see why.
• A couple of their unique specialty sushi rolls

We also ordered sashimi, which was incredibly fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared.

Parking can be a little limited since the small lot fills up quickly, but there’s additional street parking conveniently located in the neighborhood directly behind the restaurant.

Wonderful atmosphere, fresh sushi, and an overall memorable dining experience. We’ll definitely be back.

text.text:
My friend and I are visiting Austin from out of town and decided to stop at Komé for a casual lunch today because of all the on line recommendations for the restaurant. While everything was amazing, I really want to highlight the staff and, especially, our waitress (I am so sorry, I forgot your name despite asking for it a second time). She was prompt, very friendly, welcoming, and knowledgeable of the menu, giving us great suggestions when asked. Of course, all the other staff we interacted with were very friendly and helpful, as well.

As on line individuals described, the food came out quickly, while respecting our coursing, and delicious. Everything was, obviously, also of great quality despite being so affordable. We started off with the "aji fry" which was perfectly breaded, had a nice tender texture, and paired perfectly with the tartar sauce accompanying it. My friend ordered the "kitsune udon" and thoroughly enjoyed it with a side of steamed rice. I ordered the "chirashi-don", which our waitress recommended and had a variety of sashimi and definitely did not skimp out on the seafood. Everything on it was very fresh. It came with some "miso soup;" I usually don't care for miso soup, but this was very refreshing and subtle (I've had miso soup elsewhere that is too overpowering in flavor) and felt perfect as the temperatures start dropping. I also ordered the "tarantula" signature roll to share with my friend. The roll is "only" five pieces, but each piece is huge and stuffed with shrimp tempura and softshell crab. The ratio of rice to the "filling" was perfect. Definitely doable for some as a meal alone.

To end, this was a great experience and I would definitely come back if I find myself back in the Austin area. And the establishment, as amazing as the food and decor is, is very lucky to have the waitress who served us among the staff.

Kome Sushi is hands down my absolute favorite sushi spot in Austin, TX. Simply incredible and will 100% be coming back!

I started with their pork gyoza, and it was incredible. Perfectly cooked, flavorful, and a great way to kick off the meal. For sushi, I went all in with four rolls and every one of them delivered. The Crunchy Dynamite roll with spicy tuna, avocado, tempura crunch, eel sauce, and sesame seeds had the perfect balance of heat and texture. The Alone Together roll was next level with tuna, salmon, and yellowtail topped with BBQ eel, go-go sauce, eel sauce, and tempura crunch. So rich and packed with flavor. The Summertime roll with spicy tuna, shrimp tempura, avocado, go-go sauce, and sesame seeds was fresh and satisfying. My last roll, the Midnight Sun, completely blew me away. Tempura fried with smoked salmon, cream cheese, avocado, candied jalapeño, sunflower seeds, and go-go sauce. Absolute perfection with the perfect sweet and spicy kick.

Everything was fresh, beautifully prepared, and bursting with flavor. If you love sushi and are in Austin, Kome Sushi is a must. I cannot recommend this place enough.

Braised short-rib was under-seasoned, mash potatoes had several quarter size pieces, the sauce tasted of raw tomato paste.  The plating of the dish is laughable along with with the lettuce garnish.  No where near $38.  Appreciate the waiter taking 40% off the check but that won't get me to give this place another try.

text.text:
I really, really want this place to be great!  It checks so many boxes.
The first time we went, it was really good. It had a cozy, vibey, neighborhood bistro feel. Food was good!  Good enough to go back. Last night was a colossal fail. My steak was -- for lack of a more fitting term- gross!  I ordered it medium. It was served so rare it was nearly blue. My husband orders his medium-rare and he wouldn't touch it. I politely sent it back, then it came back basically gray.  Not a "well-done" gray, just a wet, rubbery gray. They had cut it in the kitchen but improperly.  When I tried to cut a bite, it was stubborn, messy and drowning in chimichurri (sp) sauce. Also, no steak knife!

It was 7p on a Saturday night and it was empty. The lighting was bright but in an otherwise dark, cozy room. It was like a bar after last call with they turn on the lights to get everyone out.   One of the servers was coughing/ hacking so much that all four of us cringed.

They comped my steak, which I appreciated. But it will be hard to get me back there.  Really bummed!

text.text:
Sammie’s in Austin is everything you hope for in a classic Italian restaurant…timeless, welcoming, and packed with unforgettable flavors. From the beautiful atmosphere to the attentive service, every part of the experience felt elevated and memorable.

The Caesar salad deserves a category of its own. It was, without question, the best Caesar salad I’ve ever had. Perfectly crisp romaine, an incredibly rich and balanced dressing, just the right amount of Parmesan, and outstanding croutons…it was so good that it could have been the main course all by itself.

The chicken piccata was another absolute standout. Tender, perfectly cooked chicken paired with a bright, buttery lemon-caper sauce that was bursting with flavor. It’s one of the best versions of this classic dish I’ve ever enjoyed.

The eggplant Parmesan was good, but compared to the other dishes, it was just OK. It was well prepared, but it didn’t quite have the same wow factor or depth of flavor as the Caesar salad and chicken piccata.

Be sure to save room for dessert because they are spectacular. Beautifully prepared, indulgent, and the perfect ending to an outstanding meal. Every bite felt like the perfect finale to an already incredible dining experience.

Between the exceptional food, outstanding service, and warm, sophisticated atmosphere, Sammie’s Italian is a restaurant that absolutely lives up to its reputation. It’s a place I’ll happily return to…and I’ll definitely be ordering that Caesar salad again.

We were really looking forward to this experience, especially since it’s so hard to get a reservation but unfortunately, it didn’t live up to the hype.
We arrived about 15 minutes early for our 8:45 reservation and were seated quickly, which was a great start. However, once seated, the noise level was overwhelming. It was so loud that I could barely understand our waitress and unfortunately didn’t catch her name or most of what she said.
We started with the mozzarella sticks, which were actually very good but at $18, definitely on the pricey side.
For my entrée, I ordered the Lumache alla vodka. The sauce was delicious with a nice little kick, but the pasta itself was undercooked to the point that I couldn’t eat it. I ended up using my husband’s pasta just to enjoy the sauce. My husband ordered the chicken parmesan, which was decent, but nothing special especially for the price. The breading was soggy, and overall, we both agreed we’ve had much better for far less.
I don’t usually send food back, but in this case, it would have been warranted. Our waitress did stop by briefly a couple of times, but the interactions were very rushed more of a quick pass through than a check in so there wasn’t a real opportunity to address the issue. Given the price point, I would have expected more attentive service.
Overall, the experience didn’t justify the cost, and it was disappointing given the expectations. Unfortunately, we won’t be returning.
We did receive free ice cream for my husband’s birthday which was much appreciated and a good way to make us feel better about the evening.

The patio out front under the glowing neon sign gave the whole evening a timeless, classic Italian feel. The Caesar salad was fresh and loaded with parmesan, the mozzarella sticks were nostalgic and delicious, and the pasta dishes were rich and comforting. Dessert sealed the deal. Sammie’s really nails that old-school Italian restaurant vibe—great food, warm service, and a relaxed but lively atmosphere. It was the perfect spot to gather the crew after a big SXSW day.

We secured a reservation through Resy for a group of three, and from the moment we arrived, the experience was seamless. The valet service was incredibly convenient and made the arrival totally stress-free.
The interior and vibe of this place are easily a 10/10—the decor and atmosphere are absolutely breathtaking and easily some of the best in the city.
As for the drinks, the Numero Uno cocktail was the star of the show! It was perfectly crafted and lived up to the hype. While the food was decent and we enjoyed trying a variety of tacos and entrees, it didn't quite reach that "wow" factor we were expecting given how incredible the setting was.
Overall, it’s a beautiful spot for a night out with family, especially if you appreciate a gorgeous environment and a killer signature drink! 🌮

text.text: I’ve been to Fonda San Miguel several times and I feel like the experience from when I first came here many years ago until now has changed. It’s definitely become more famous undoubtedly. The few recent times that I have come, I felt like we were treated like a number and not a patron. No one has necessarily been rude to us (meaning either my friends or my family) when we’ve been there but it just does not feel hospitable. This last time I came with a couple of friends and the waiter greeted us warmly. He was very kind at first, but as the night went on, we felt forgotten and rushed. He didn’t really come by to check on us often and when we were done paying the bill, we had to wait for my friends rideshare to come. As we sat there, he started removing the chips, salsa., & the drinks. It really just didn’t feel kind. I also felt like the table near us got more attention than we did. Again, I do not think they were rude at all. But I also didn’t feel like a valued & appreciated patron. I’m sure other friends and family will want to visit here because it’s so popular, but I really don’t have high expectations anytime I visit.

By far one of the worst experiences in a long time. This was actually my second time giving Fonda San Miguel a chance. The first time I went with a friend and didn’t have a great experience, so I had already told my husband to keep expectations low but we decided to try it again anyway given they had few veggie options.

This time we ordered the veggie enchiladas and the sweet potato appetizer. The enchiladas (Suiza and mole) were fine, but nothing memorable or impressive. The mango margarita was also pretty average. The appetizer also didn’t taste any good it was just boiled/friend potatoes with light sauce.

What really made the experience most disappointing was the service from our server Maury (this was the name on receipt not sure if that was his name )

He seemed noticeably warmer, more attentive to other tables addressing them with smiles and checking every now and then especially larger parties, while being super cold and distant with us. It felt like clear preferential treatment, and it definitely left a bad impression. It was so evident that I was compelled to leave a note on my receipt something I had never done before.

Overall, the food was just okay, but the service made the experience worse. After two tries, this just isn’t a place I’d go back to.

⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ (4/5)

My girlfriend and I recently visited Justine’s for a date night, and overall we had a great experience. The atmosphere is charming, romantic, and has a unique East Austin vibe that makes it a perfect spot for a night out.

We both ordered the Steak Frites. She chose the herb sauce, while I went with the sauce au poivre. The steaks were cooked well, flavorful, and definitely the highlight of the meal. I also enjoyed a glass of the Dacite Chilled Red Wine, which paired nicely with dinner.

Service was attentive, and the ambiance alone makes this place worth visiting. While the meal wasn’t quite a perfect 10/10 for me, it was still very enjoyable. I’d give the steak an 8/10 and would absolutely return to try more items from the menu.

A great spot for date night, good food, and a memorable dining experience. Highly recommend checking it out if you’re in East Austin. 🍷🥩✨

text.text:
TLDR: Great for apps and drinks, not for mains. Service and seating left a lot to be desired — but there's enough here to give it another shot.

Visited 3/5/26 @ 8:30pm — reservation made a week in advance with a birthday note in the booking. They seated us directly in front of the hallway to the bathrooms and kitchen. Music blasting right above us. Our server had no idea we were celebrating anything. Not a great start.

The lump crab salad was a miss. Mostly thinly sliced cucumbers with scattered dollops of crab hiding in the crevices — my friend described it as cucumbers with tajin. Mint added freshness but it's not worth the price. The tuna tartare was good, slightly over sauced. The octopus was nicely cooked but there were only two small tentacles on the plate. Escargots were overcooked and tough, but garlic butter saves everything.

The mains were where it fell apart. The pork chop came out hot but was dry and almost inedible — the butter sauce and potatoes au gratin were the only saving grace, and the gratin was genuinely lovely. The steak frites was fine, cooked better than the pork, but tiny. We also waited a noticeable stretch for new utensils between courses.

Dessert redeemed things slightly. The mille-feuille had a beautifully thin, light pastry with vanilla cream that wasn't overly sweet. The fig sorbet didn't taste much like fig but was very pleasant regardless.

I'd still like to return as there were other items on the menu I wanted to try. Food also came out in a timely manner. The mains need refining.

Would recommend:
Potatoes au gratin
Mille-feuille
Get a table in the tent — too loud inside

Skip:
Lump crab salad
Pork chop
Tuna tartare
Escargots

text.text: I’ve never wanted to eat in one of those fancy Micheline Star restaurants. Thought it was cliche—like a marketing gimmick. Today, I walk into Maie Day, and there it is—well almost. It’s a red plaque that has the word Micheline on it. Turns out they’re on the waiting list to  get one. Anyway, what the heck. I’m here; let’s eat. I order the NY strip and a kale salad. The dishes came and they were delicious. The steak was finished off with that fancy French salt—fleur de sel, yummy stuff. Only disappointment was my steak was slightly overcooked. I ordered medium and got closer to medium well. Still really good though. Have fun.

text.text:
Overall, Este landed squarely in the middle for me - a 6/10. We ordered a good spread to get a feel for the menu: tuna tiradito, fish taco, camarones "El Ricas," and cochinita pibil.

The tuna tiradito kicked things off on a high note - it tasted super fresh, and the avocado paired with it beautifully. Next up, the swordfish taco had a great crispy crunch, though the fish itself leaned a bit too fishy for my taste. The camarones were juicy and flavorful, but I wanted bolder, richer notes; given the description, they played it a little too safe. As for the cochinita pibil, it was tender and juicy, but ultimately not all that memorable.

On the plus side, the vibe was lively and the service was friendly, which made for a pleasant atmosphere. But given the premium price point, I left expecting more punch from the flavors and the overall experience. If you're set on trying Este, I'd definitely recommend hitting up happy hour for better value. One small but notable gripe: for a restaurant in this tier, I also expected the restrooms to be much cleaner - it's a detail that shouldn't be overlooked at these prices.

text.text:
Este is like a food adventure straight to coastal Mexico. In addition, AnnaMaria was able to mark up a menu with the chef for the Gluten Free and Celiac safe items.

The Cold Bar offerings are sooo good and refreshing. From ceviche to agua chile, these dishes are a perfect starter or meal on a hot sunny day.

When you move on to some warm dishes, the Ricas, a red chile shrimp dish is spot on! We also enjoyed a wagyu ribeye taco which hit some strong umami notes.

The Meloncito is not listed as a dessert but AnnaMaria recommended it to finish out the meal. It was a perfect finish to a celebration of coastal cuisine.

Reservations are recommended but not required. We had a rez through Open Table.

text.text:
Phenomenal food and service but the noise levels are quite loud. It's warranted though since this establishment was filled with people, so I suggest booking a reservation to secure a spot.

Everything was great, from the starter to the dessert. The half portion ceviche is a great decision because it allows a solo diner (like me) to enjoy more items on the menu. You can expect each device bite to be fresh, tangy, and slightly spicy. The Cachetada and Bokchoy both also had deep flavours, but are quite overpriced for their portions.

I came here to find the best seafood spots in the area, and I think the Pescado a la crema delivered. The halibut completely melted in my mouth and was enriched with the salsa cremosa. The baby shrimps adds a nice texture and the squash completed the smoothness of the entree. The dish is still on the smallef end, so ordering starters dishes are necessary to acquire fullness.

The Pineapple Tarte was suggested by my waitress Chelsea. The item did not intrigue me on the menu, but the recommendation completely proved me wrong. It is like a slightly milder Key Lime Pie, but with a smoother yet still denser texture. With the crumble bottom adding a nice crunch, the dessert wonderfully wrapped my experience at Este.

The dishes can be adjusted to your preference, which is the cherry on the top to come back for more. I can't wait to share this soot with my friends and family.

text.text: Inventive Mexican seafood-centric cuisine. It was our first visit and we didn’t know what to expect. We were blown away. The food was innovative and expertly done. The family style (think tapas sizes) servings made for ample conversations and comparisons on what we enjoyed best. For a family of four with two young children we got 5 smaller plates and 2 large plates. Some of our faves were the Camarones el Ricas (grilled shrimp), Tuna Tiradito, ceviche  and the pescado à la crema (think filet of fish in an elevated lobster bisque sauce. The sauces were stars of the show although it made the meal quite heavy we didn’t have room for deserts. Don’t over stuff on the tortilla chips to start save the room for the good stuff. Although we have to admit the guacamole was super yummy and different from what we can get in NYC. There  are few non fish dishes but the seafood is the reason to visit. Complimentary valet parking makes life super easy also. We highly recommend.

text.text:
What an incredible dining experience at Canje — honestly even better than we hoped for.

Planning a Friday night dinner date in Austin can sometimes feel impossible with how busy the city gets, especially at some of the more popular restaurants. My wife and I decided to take the chance anyway, and from the moment we arrived, everything about the evening exceeded expectations. First of all, we were—surprisingly, able to get a table right away.

The atmosphere was vibrant, colorful, welcoming, and incredibly LGBTQ+ friendly and inclusive, which immediately made us feel comfortable and excited to settle in for the evening. The décor itself is such an experience — energetic, artistic, and thoughtfully designed without feeling overwhelming.

The service was absolutely phenomenal. Huge thank you to Steph for making our night feel special from start to finish with attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable service.

The food was unforgettable. Every dish was layered with bold flavor combinations, vibrant spices, and textures that felt unique and thoughtfully crafted. We ordered the coconut rice, coconut rolls, avocado appetizer, wild boar pepper pot, and the roti — and the roti is an absolute must-order. It was buttery, flaky, rich, and easily one of the most memorable flatbreads I’ve had in Austin. Note: This amount of food was more than enough for the two of us and we ended up with leftovers—remember, you can always add more.

One helpful tip for anyone visiting: the dedicated parking lot is very small and fills up quickly, especially on weekends and Friday evenings, but there are several nearby paid parking options within walking distance that make it manageable. There’s also a valet if you don’t want to mess with finding a space.

This was one of those restaurant experiences where the food, atmosphere, and service all aligned perfectly. Canje absolutely lives up to the hype, and we’re already looking forward to returning to explore more of the menu.

What a gem of a restaurant. Sitting at the counter we had a perfect view of the choreographed operations of the kitchen and got a masterclass in restaurant kitchen operations. Amazing to see all the orders getting cooked in that kitchen. Their wood fired oven is their center of operations and making me thing that I need one too:-).  Our seating at the counter also allowed us access to the Chef Chelsea who was such a gracious host and wonderful to speak to.

My burger was just awesome. The meat combination they used was well balanced and the fries were also perfectly crisp outside and soft inside. The starwberry pie was unique since it was not the usual crust but used the puff pastry mix and well balanced with their scoop of home made ice cream.

We were kind of not sure of going there since we had no reservation and walkin required 45 minute due to today being Friday but we are so glad we went. It was well worth the wait and rewarding.

We tried the esquites, which had a nice char and a little kick. The tostada with pickled carrots was fresh and flavorful, but the blue corn pancakes were definitely the highlight of the meal. Drinks were just okay.

Overall, great ambiance and a really nice spot for brunch, especially if you can get patio seating. Definitely recommend making reservations.

We tried several dishes including the guacamole, the crudo, the carnitas tacos, the chicken a la brasa, and the churros, and all of them were absolutely delicious. Everything was flavorful and the overall dining experience was fantastic.

Unfortunately, a few hours after our dinner on Wednesday night, I became very sick with severe stomach issues that persisted for several days, culminating in a visit to emergency care for dehydration and treatment. I can’t say for certain what caused it, but I wanted to share this feedback in case it’s helpful for the restaurant to be aware and look into.

Aside from that situation, the service, ambiance, and overall experience at the restaurant were excellent. The service we received from Mike was exceptional and his recommendations were spot on and made our experience really enjoyable.

Walked in on a Saturday evening hoping to get a table for two and were initially told there would be a two-hour wait. We decided to check the bar area and, after about 15 minutes, were able to grab a table there instead.

Overall, the food was good, though I enjoyed some dishes more than others. The short rib quesadilla (6/10) was my least favorite — it was quite greasy and lacked flavor. The tostada de tinga (8/10) was much better: very flavorful and well-balanced. The queso flameado (7/10) was also tasty and came in a generous portion. The churros were the highlight of the meal (9/10) — absolutely delicious.

I’d definitely recommend making a reservation next time to avoid the long wait, but overall it was a solid dining experience.

text.text:
Comedor lives up to its reputation as one of Austin's trendiest dining destinations. The space is stunning—an industrial warehouse aesthetic, dramatic natural light, and a sleek, modern vibe that makes the whole experience feel special.

The menu is designed for sharing, with small plates that feel more like modern Mexican tapas than a traditional meal. Portions are on the smaller side, but ordering a variety of dishes makes for a fun experience.

It's been a few weeks since our visit, so I can't remember every flavor in detail, but one dish stood out to everyone at the table: the crispy potatoes. They were unexpectedly the star of the meal—perfectly crisp on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and incredibly flavorful. We liked them so much that we ended up ordering a second bowl.

text.text:
I’ll get to those bone marrow tacos in a moment… First off, my wife chose Comedor to celebrate my recent birthday. Can I mention my wife is brilliant and beautiful?
The space is quite stunning. A discreet side door opens into a sophisticated mix of industrial grit with spacious open-air minimalism. That sounds cold and forbidding, but it’s quite the opposite.
We started with carefully crafted cocktails. The Isla Privada (vodka, aperol, passionfruit, pineapple, lemon, and bitters) and the Comedor Margarita (blanco tequila, citrus-blend, cointreau) were perfectly balanced and refreshing. We tried two crudo dishes: the Aguachile (kanpachi, chile costeño rojo & citrus broth, apple, cucumber, charred allium) and the Spicy Tuna Crudo (yellowfin tuna, coconut-culichi salsa, fried shallots, habanero). Both were unique and delicious.
Next were the bone marrow tacos. I haven’t had bone marrow in a while but always enjoy it when I see it on a menu. This preparation was something I’ve never experienced. The marrow is roasted with smoked butter and served on top of sautéed quelites (wild greens). The contrast of the savory marrow with the slightly bitter greens was the perfect balance. What makes them very inventive is the pecan gremolata. This added an unexpected crunch that worked perfectly. They are served alongside delicious homemade corn tortillas. The only thing I would add is that the greens did get stuck in my teeth, but we were happy to see toothpicks in the restrooms! It’s pretty clear why these tacos are one of the signature dishes.
We finished with the Dean & Peeler NY Strip steak served with chilhuacle negro butter and herbs. It was cooked a perfect medium-rare and was melt-in-your-mouth perfect.
Our server was Bryan, and he was outstanding. He was polite, engaging, and attentive. His thoughtful suggestions were spot on and his pacing of dishes was flawless. An added surprise was a birthday card signed by all of the staff, delivered with two glasses of prosecco. I suppose it’s a good sign that days later we are still talking about our experience.

text.text:
Comedor continues to be one of our favorite dining experiences in Austin. The food is incredible—thoughtful, creative, and full of flavor without ever feeling overcomplicated. Every dish feels intentional, highlighting great ingredients and letting them shine naturally.

What really stood out on our visit was the hospitality from the bar team. They was welcoming, knowledgeable, and genuinely cared about making our experience special. From their cocktail recommendations to the overall service, everything felt effortless and authentic. You can tell there's a strong culture of hospitality here, and it really elevate an already amazing meal.

Great food is easy to find in Austin. Great food paired with service that makes you want to come back is much harder to find. Comedor delivers both every time.

text.text: This place is a nice little spot, with seating inside and nice on the front patio as well (hopefully they get more comfortable chairs for the inside one day) Its a nice vibe and pretty solid spot for a date. The service was pretty good and they were all nice and very accommodating. I wanted to give the food 5 star because some of it i do rate very highly but some others weren't quite there. To start the shrimp cocktail was good, the shrimp are massive and both sauces served with them are good as well. Bills burger (no tomato and grill the onions) is a Top 5 burger I have ever had, the patties are made with brisket and short rib and those things are flavor packed, and you combine that with great cheese, sauce and a great bun and its hard to beat. The chicken fried steak was a bit on the tougher side but not terrible, and the crawfish Mac & cheese was solid but not quite as good as I expected but was still solid for sure. I cant wait to go back and try more stuff! The burger I give a 9.0/10 and Overall I give the place an 8.1/10

text.text: One of the best happy hours and burgers in Austin!! We came in on Wednesday at 5pm without a reservation and they were so welcoming and found us a seat by the window where there was great people-watching. I will definitely be making a reservation next time we dine here because this place is popular during happy hour and I can see why. We had the raw oysters from the east coast, clams michelada, tuna tartar, hush puppies, burger with fries, dirty gin martini, and a bottle of wine (50% off during happy hour!) I strongly recommend the raw oysters, burger with fries, and tuna tartar as well as the martinis. Really loved the food, atmosphere, and staff. We will be back!

We ordered the lobster rolls and crab cake. I'd say the lobster roll was decent but not spectacular. I prefer main style lobster rolls which has mayo and celery. Connecticut lobster rolls are also popular which is mostly butter. Clark's lobster roll combines both styles and i felt it overpowered the lobster. The lobster was high quality and fresh and I liked the roll it was served on. They do not offer gluten free bread options. I have a love-hate relationship with their fries, I love shoe string fries but they are really hard to eat and it is awkward to eat them in a nicer dining setting. Thr crab cake was entirely crab and i could not taste any breading, no complaints there. I would much rather get a lobster roll from here where in a elevated ambiance than a food truck, especially when the price difference is miniminal.

A major negative is that the lettuce the lobster was served on was not washed properly, it has dirt on it.

We had some truly standout dishes at Clark’s. The oysters were next‑level—fresh, clean, and incredibly delicious.

The crab Louie was another highlight: bright, flavorful, and beautifully done. The fries were honestly addictive crispy, salty, and impossible to stop eating. And the crab cake was rich, decadent, and perfectly executed.

The service was great, and they have a fantastic wine list with plenty of options that pair perfectly with seafood.

A couple of things didn’t quite hit the mark for us: the stone crab wasn’t our favorite, and the lobster roll bread was on the dry side, which took away from the dish.

Overall, Clark’s has a lot to love, with excellent dishes, great service, and a strong wine list just a few tweaks needed on a couple of items

Dinner at Clark’s last night and it absolutely delivered.

The lobster roll was excellent and the oysters were delicious — we had a mix from New Brunswick and Massachusetts that were fresh and briny in the best way. The real surprise of the night was the ceviche, which might honestly be the best I’ve ever had.

Around the table, the burger got rave reviews, the crispy salmon with polenta was really good, and the linguini with clams was a big hit as well.

Drinks were great too — a crisp local pilsner from Meanwhile Brewing and a fantastic mocktail.

Add in wonderful service and the whole experience felt relaxed, polished, and genuinely enjoyable. A great night out all around.

We actually haven’t been back in a few years (no specific reason - it’s just a bit of a distance from us) but after this last trip, we may need to make Odd Duck part of our regular rotation 🤤.

I had an incredible experience at Top Roe! The quality of the fish was outstanding—especially the hamachi, scallops, and tuna, which were unbelievably fresh and flavorful. Every bite melted in my mouth, and the texture and taste were just perfect.

The ambiance was intimate yet lively, making it a great spot for both a casual night out and a special occasion. The service was also top-notch—attentive without being intrusive.

I particularly loved how the seaweed in the hand rolls was super crispy, adding a great texture contrast. The balance of flavors and attention to detail in each dish made it clear that the chefs here truly care about their craft.

If you’re a sushi lover in Austin, Top Roe is a must-visit! I’ll definitely be back soon.

It was acceptable cost wise because we got many items from the HH, but if we paid full price, I wouldn’t return. I like that they tell you “the seats are for 1:15 hour” at checkin, but also this is a very quick meal, takes away from the experience.

The hamachi sashimi was amazing! The bluefin tuna was good if you got some of the sauce. Hand roll wise, we liked the crunchy tuna, shrimp tempura, and uni. The dessert was good too.

Don’t waste money on the trinity.

Would recommend making a reservation before you come. Parking is slightly difficult to find since it’s a very tiny parking lot.

As for the food, the vegetarian pastas were amazing. Our server was very sweet and marked all the vegetarian options on the menu for us. We got the Potato pasta and the one with corn and oh my both were amazing. The flavors were so unique and so good for a pasta. The pizza however was a little underwhelming. We got the arrabbiata and the zucchini one and both were lacking in flavor.

They brought us some of their artisanal chocolates that they make in house to try and it was delicious. It was a dark chocolate with salt and it was one of the best pieces of chocolate I have ever tried. Then for dessert we had the gooey cake with cinnamon gelato and I have to say it was one of the best desserts I’ve ever had. The warm meringue and the cinnamon gelato go perfectly with the gooey cake.

Ambiance was very classy and is perfect for a date night or a birthday dinner.

It’s a standout dining experience that has maintained its quality and creativity over the years.

text.text:
In a city that takes its food seriously, Bartlett’s on West Anderson Lane has quietly built one of the most dependable and satisfying dining experiences in Austin. This is the kind of place that reminds you what a great neighborhood restaurant is supposed to feel like, warm, genuine, and consistently excellent every single time you walk through the door.

The food is simply great. The menu is fresh and inspired, with standouts that earn serious repeat visits. Whether you are in the mood for something hearty or something lighter, the kitchen delivers with care and precision. This is not a place that dazzles you once and lets you down the next time. Consistency is clearly a point of pride here, and it shows on every plate.

The staff is what really sets Bartlett’s apart. Attentive without being intrusive, knowledgeable without being pretentious, these are people who genuinely enjoy what they do, and that energy is contagious. Whether you are dropping in solo, bringing the family, hosting a business lunch, or celebrating something special, the team here makes every guest feel like the visit matters.

Bartlett’s has earned its place as one of Austin’s go-to dining destinations. It is the kind of restaurant you recommend without hesitation, return to without needing a reason, and trust completely. If you have not been, fix that soon.

text.text:
Suerte is hands down one of the best Mexican restaurants in Austin and absolutely worth visiting.

First, make a reservation. The place is not very big, and it gets busy for a reason. But once you’re in, the experience is excellent from start to finish.

The menu is full of authentic, well-executed Mexican flavors. We tried quite a few dishes, and overall, everything was very good to outstanding.

The suadero tacos are a must honestly unforgettable. The tacos al pastor were another highlight; they were so good we ended up ordering more. The huitlacoche quesadillas were a real delicacy, rich and full of flavor. The tlayuda with mushrooms was also delicious, and the ceviche was fresh and really enjoyable.

We also tried the black mole flautas, which were good but honestly not as impressive as the other dishes.

For drinks, the margaritas were excellent and perfectly balanced.

We also had a lamb/barbacoa-style dish served with warm tortillas, which added a comforting, traditional touch to the meal.

Overall, this is a Mexican restaurant that truly delivers on quality, flavor, and experience. It’s one of those places where you feel every dollar is well spent. Highly recommended you will not regret going.

Best meal of the Austin trip: upscale tacos and housemade masa in a welcoming space.

Food: 5 Service: 4.5 Atmosphere: 5
Cost to worth it rating: 3
Opentableable: yes
Return worthiness: yes

Highlights:
- Waitress Kelly was wonderful and so professional. She noticed I was ordering dairy items on side and asked about if pesto in guacamole  was ok. So astute and kind of her. Also on my friends second drink remembered she didn't want salt or her rim without even asking
- Everything tasted so fresh and high quality
- Brisket tacos: packed with flavor--maybe it was the wagyu meat or the black magic oil. Freshly made corn tortillas were awesome. Usually corn ones and pretty throwaway meh, but these added to the greatness of the tacos. 5 stars
- Duck flautas: crispy covered in mild mole. Loved the mashed potato addition inside for some mellowness and texture. 5 stars
- Guacamole: so fresh and that dollop of pesto on top was lovely. Served with crispy masa dippers were impressive almost a 8x11 page size. It was fun to crack off into pieces, but hard to stop eating it. 5 stars
- Sweet potato: friend loved these long charred wedges. 4.5 stars
- Cocktails were stellar. I got the Don Dario which was a play on a marg and delightful
- $12 of a few drinks during lucky hour (Mon-Fri 5-6pm, Sat-Sun 3-5pm)
- High energy vibes in a clean, open, tan colored space
- Had their bottle water on the table in a champagne bottle which speaks to my heart

Midlights:
- In East Austin so have to Uber if you are staying more central
- Tacos come in orders of 4. Wish it was less so we could've tried more variety.

Lowlights
- No food discounts for lucky hour
- Didn't have time to try the choco taco which looked amaze
- Large gap of time between items first few items coming out and the rest

I really liked this place!

It was such a fun lunch spot to celebrate my friend being pregnant. As random as that may sound, this place provided that kind of ambiance that was a destination feel.

Everything we had was very delicious, & full of color. The reason why I did not give the food a five star was because I felt that the guacamole lacked a tiny bit of salt and the portion of the pickled veggies was larger than the portion of guac itself. I understand the prices and don’t mind paying, but it felt very skimpy for what it was.

The beverages were so delicious. I personally had the watermelon juice and the green juice and love them both. We also has the Aguachile, chicken and beef fajitas for the table. For three of us, we were able to eat all that and feel very full and satiated.

As I mentioned, we were there to celebrate my friend being pregnant, and the server was so kind enough to give us these nonalcoholic celebration shots. She also brought over some churros, which we were very grateful for and really appreciated. The touch she gave.

Service was phenomenal. Everything was great and I highly recommend coming to this place.

text.text:
La Piscina, located in the beautiful and eclectic Austin Proper Hotel, offers a stunning rooftop setting that makes for a memorable brunch experience. Our group of four was seated on their patio, which was both picturesque and comfortable in temperature.

We were welcomed with freshly made tortilla chips and two house salsas, which set a strong first impression. The cocktails were equally impressive - creative, well-balanced, and beautifully presented. That said, service was inconsistent. It took about 20 minutes to receive our drinks after ordering them, and after they arrived, we didn’t see our server again for another 20 minutes. As a result, we didn’t place our food order until roughly 45 minutes after being seated. It seemed like our server may have been having an off day.

Once ordered, the food arrived promptly and it absolutely delivered. While La Piscina is known for its sizzling fajitas (which we’d definitely recommend), the standout for us was the gulf snapper aguachile -- savory, bright, and incredibly refreshing. The pastry basket was another highlight, with baked goods that were moist and just the right level of sweet.

A couple of notes for future diners: table space on the patio tables is fairly tight, especially when sharing dishes like fajitas, which made things feel a bit cramped. Additionally, despite the hotel’s website noting a partnership with MML Hospitality, MML gift cards are no longer accepted. We had called ahead to confirm and were still surprised to learn this upon trying to pay our bill.

Overall, La Piscina shines in ambiance and food quality, but the service and a few logistical details left room for improvement.

This is a spot I lusted after for a very long time and never tried while living in Austin, so when the opportunity came to try during a recent visit I was so excited and F+D delivered the experience I was craving and then some:)

Our server Kunika was so genuinely friendly and conversational, she gave us some great recommendations for wine to pair with the $1 East Coast oyster special (we went for a salt-forward white), and was so present and attentive! All other servers we interacted with were on the same wavelength, making for the most pleasant service experience!

We paired the oysters with Crispy Fingerlings, Gruyere Popovers, Parisian Gnocchi, and Melted Leek Risotto. All of which were exactly what you’d expect, absolutely phenomenal. The popovers and fingerlings were yummy and complexly savory little accoutrements, while both the gnocchi and risotto were absolutely melt in your mouth umami takes on pasta dishes

F+D is so worth the splurge, I can’t believe I waited so long to try!

text.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ A Standout Sushi Experience

I had an exceptional meal at Neighborhood Sushi. The variety and execution of the dishes made it clear this place takes its craft seriously. We ordered a wide range of items, and not a single plate missed.

The Secret Garden and To Saturn and Back were creative, balanced, and beautifully presented. The Broccolini Tempura and Truffled Beech Mushroom Tempura hit that perfect light-crispy texture without feeling heavy, and the Corn Kakiage was surprisingly addictive.

Nigiri was the real highlight. The Sea Bream, Tasmanian Trout, Fluke, Japanese Western, and 2 King Crab Nigiri were all incredibly fresh, expertly cut, and seasoned with just the right touch—no soy sauce needed. Even the house-made Kizami Wasabi stood out.

The hot items were equally strong: the Basil Shrimp Tempura was delicate and flavorful, the Amberjack Crudo was bright and clean, and the Fish Collar was rich, tender, and perfectly charred.

Cocktails were thoughtful as well—The Rising Sun and Red Dragon Cocktail both paired perfectly with the food without overpowering it.

Service from Tomas was smooth and attentive throughout, and the whole experience felt relaxed but elevated. With the amount and quality of food we ordered, the value felt absolutely justified.

If you want sushi that’s both creative and technically precise, this place is a must. I’d come back in a heartbeat.

The atmosphere is truly special: gorgeous vintage-inspired interiors, green tile, leather Chesterfield couches, and beautiful natural light. It was a hot Austin day, but the space stayed wonderfully cool and comfortable the entire time.

The staff really knows their menu. They made fantastic recommendations on both cocktails and food, and everything we tried was a hit (the pretzel is a must-order). Our group had an amazing time, and the team handled our event seamlessly.

I’ll absolutely be back — and I’m already looking forward to booking the space for future events. Highly recommend for date nights, group gatherings, or private events alike!

text.text:
The staff always spoils me when I come through. They offer a phenomenal tasting menu, but you can also order à la carte.

The wine menu is my favorite aspect - I can find some real old-world wines in the cellar that are decently priced and pair beautifully with their dishes. They also have excellent by-the-glass options and well-crafted cocktails. My wife’s favorite is a drink they serve on fire tableside - it’s quite an experience if you’ve never seen it done.

One of the most memorable experiences I’ve had at Hestia speaks to their attention to detail: on my first visit, I mentioned I only drink bottled water. They didn’t have any available, so I just drank my Sauvignon Blanc to quench my thirst. The next time I returned, they had taken notes and specifically bought Mountain Valley bottled water for me. They remembered and made sure they had some on hand when I came through. That kind of thoughtful, personalized service is what sets exceptional restaurants apart.

If you’re looking for a tasting menu experience in Austin, this is it. Great ambiance, upscale atmosphere - dress up and come have a wonderful time. Hestia delivers on every level.

text.text:
My wife and I made a visit to Hestia during our trip to Austin. We primarily chose this restaurant because it was part of the Chase Sapphaire Open Tables. We made a reservation for the bar as we like to sit at the bar to enjoy conversations with the bar tenders.

When we arrived, we were promptly greeted and sat at the bar. The service at the bar was really good, and we given a complementary champange when we arrived. Our reservations were later, and the place was mostly empty.

We really enjoyed the entrance of the restaruant and the overall vibe, it felt very industrial and seemed to fit the area well. My wife started with a dirty martini which she is very particular about and really enjoyed it.

We started with the charred corn and scallops, both were very good and presented and plated nicely. We were also served bread and butter. The bread was very good, and the butter was perfectly salted. For mains, we opted for the Red Ranger Chicken and Halibut, both mains were also very nicely presented and had good flavor.

Our only complaint is that we had planned on sharing the mains, but the Halibut arrived much sooner than the chicken and we had to wait some time for the chicken to arrive.

For a Michelin star resturant, we felt the value was worth it and we will definetly visit again when we are in Austin.

The sourdough ice cream is very different and had a great mix of sweetness, saltiness and sourness - something you’d not get at a lot of places.

text.text: Excellent food, cocktails, atmosphere, and service. It’s not hard to see why it’s on the Michelin guide. We visited with two toddlers early on a Saturday evening and were treated very well. It wasn’t quite busy nor very loud at that point, so it worked well. The drinks were creative and delicious. Lovely plating for each of the dishes, and everything was served at a perfect temperature. They even had a well-lit single bathroom with a lovely changing table available, which I didn’t expect but certainly appreciated. The staff were all very kind and accommodating, and the service was fast and efficient. Drinks from the bar came quickly and looked as good as they tasted. Portions were quite large for the price and quality level in my opinion. The steak dish and ceviche in particular felt quite generously sized — certainly enough for two to four to share if you’re eating family-style. We ordered three appetizers / tapas and one “main” and could barely finish.
